guard.name: The desk
guard.why: The MoMA Guard, No. 625, stands next to his own portrait. He never moves.

works.s: He stands eight hours between you and a masterpiece. The watchful eye, the corner post, the quiet do not touch

lobby.name: The lobby wall
lobby.why: Four anchors from the founding eras: what the curator would hang first.

works.s: Golden off the boardwalk, split open with a stripe of mustard laid like a boulevard. Deli paper for a throne, steam for a crown
She points at the zebra board at every stop to prove she is watching. A saint's icon in the cab window, the whole platform in bloom
A flower with a human iris pushes up through a subway grate at dawn. Where a dreamer's tear fell a century ago, a tiny crowned rat witnessing
The Rat King married the Pigeon Queen beneath the bridge at midnight, fireflies for ushers. A bottle cap crown exchanged for an iridescent feather, two kingdoms united above and below

f2_west.name: The Trait Layer and The MLow Show
f2_west.why: Eras XVIII and XIX, the newest work, hung the way MoMA hangs its contemporary floor: big, few, and lit from above.

works.t: Halyna Yakovlev, a woman who runs a warehouse party with the chart projected on the wall
works.s: Halyna runs a warehouse party with the chart projected on the wall. A livery cab window with the bridge behind, going home

works.t: Everton Charlemagne, a street photographer with a rangefinder on a Bronx platform
works.s: Everton works a Bronx platform with a rangefinder and no permission. A rangefinder raised to the eye, the train arriving

works.t: Consuelo Villanueva, a collector who spends a fixed share of every sale on other artists
works.s: Consuelo spends a fixed share of every sale on other artists. Two other people on a call, confirming the split

works.t: Danuta Yakovlev, a woman who quit her job on a number and is watching it fall
works.s: Danuta quit her job on a number and is watching it fall. A school desk and nine faces leaning in, her new job

works.t: Folasade Diallo, a woman who sings a jingle into a phone before every recording
works.s: Folasade sings the same jingle into her phone before every recording. A boom over two stools, a ritual nobody else knows

works.t: Lhakpa Gurung, a man who borrowed against a piece and is now watching the price
works.s: Lhakpa borrowed against a piece and is watching the price. A phone face down under one flat hand, watching anyway

works.t: Ming-hua Ishikawa, a collector who bought an artist early purely because she liked it
works.s: Ming-hua bought the artist early because she liked the work. A projector throws it on plaster, still liked

works.t: Yaa Camara, a painter watching a countdown at a kitchen table in Astoria at midnight
works.s: Yaa watches the countdown at her kitchen table in Astoria at midnight. A blank glowing screen and the number falling toward zero

works.t: Kelvin Hollins, a man whose piece was removed from a platform and later reinstated
works.s: Kelvin's piece was removed from a platform and later reinstated. A chain link fence with prints wired to it

works.t: Eli Shulman, a person who has been in the same server for five years
works.s: Eli has been in the same server for five years. An office bathroom stall and a phone, his desk

works.t: Chidi Danquah, a sculptor who prints the 3D file in bronze
works.s: Chidi prints the 3D file in bronze. Red and cyan edges doubled around the sculpture

works.t: Nadia Chalabi, a woman who is the only sober person in a group chat at four
works.s: Nadia is the only sober person in a group chat at four. A coffee gone cold hours ago, the only one

works.t: Ngawang Thapa, a man who reads a contract aloud at a gallery
works.s: Ngawang reads a contract aloud at a gallery. A cage of servers with one green status light, listening

works.t: Vikram Chowdhury, an artist who lets a piece sit at a known price for nine months
works.s: Vikram let the piece sit at a known price for nine months. A countdown on a blank glowing screen finally started

works.t: Aileen Fenwick, an artist who ran the image through a free glitch tool and told everyone
works.s: Aileen ran the image through a free glitch tool and told everyone. A slider dragged until the face slides off

works.t: Pearline Achille, a preparator building crates for digital work
works.s: Pearline builds crates for digital work. A generator running in an alley behind the workshop

works.t: Yun Zhang, a man watching a candle at four in the morning in a Flushing internet cafe
works.s: Yun watches a candle at four in the morning in a Flushing internet cafe. A livery cab window with the bridge behind at dawn

works.t: Salvatore Halloran, a kid who turned a meme into rent
works.s: Salvatore turned a meme into rent. A livery cab window with the bridge behind, the month paid

works.t: Maureen Fairweather, a woman who trades from the back of a livery cab across the bridge
works.s: Maureen trades from the back of a livery cab across the bridge. A chart projected on a warehouse wall at the other end

works.t: Jamyang Wangdu, a trader who funds an artist with the winnings and never tells them
works.s: Jamyang funds an artist with the winnings and never tells them. A livery cab window with the bridge behind, the cheque sent

works.t: Hipolito Almonte, a man who took the profit and bought a painting
works.s: Hipolito took the profit and bought a painting. A livery cab window with the bridge behind, the painting in his lap

works.t: Shanice Bridges, a woman who trades from the back of a livery cab across the bridge
works.s: Shanice trades from the back of a livery cab across the bridge. A full drink and a loss waiting at the bar

works.t: Bo Chow, a founder doing a livestream while it happens
works.s: Bo does a livestream while it happens. A rooftop speaker and a string of lights, the audience watching him watch

works.t: Icilda Springer, a woman who photographs from a moving car window across the bridge
works.s: Icilda photographs from a moving car window across the bridge. A rangefinder raised to the eye at forty miles an hour

works.t: Pearline Pierre-Louis, a woman who launched a coin from a bodega and watched it go
works.s: Pearline launched a coin from a bodega and watched it go. A chart projected on a warehouse wall, the bodega famous

works.t: Nour Barakat, a woman who set a rule and broke it the same night
works.s: Nour set a rule and broke it the same night. A coffee gone cold hours ago, the rule with it

works.t: Aminata Sanogo, a bartender at last call who knows every ticker by the faces
works.s: Aminata tends bar at last call and knows every ticker by the faces. Coloured lights on a boat deck on her night off

works.t: Nechama Katzenberg, a technician who runs the plotters for everybody
works.s: Nechama runs the plotters for everybody. A pen that has run dry mid draw, somebody else's

works.t: Leah Feldman, a woman who has told nobody at all
works.s: Leah has told nobody at all. A torch and a spade in a yard at night, nobody watching

works.t: Khin Bautista, a woman who photographs garbage night on the East Village sidewalk as source
works.s: Khin photographs garbage night as source and nothing else. A soldering iron and a glowing tube on the desk

works.t: Franco Donnelly, an artist watching strangers decide what a year of work is worth
works.s: Franco watches strangers decide what a year of work is worth. A rooftop speaker and a string of lights, the verdict soon

works.t: Svetlana Zielinski, a collector who bought the piece that got thrown off the platform
works.s: Svetlana bought the piece that got thrown off the platform. Two other people on a call, confirming it was real

works.t: Segun Balogun, a man who builds every portrait in red and cyan so it stands off the wall
works.s: Segun builds every portrait in red and cyan so it stands off the wall. Red and cyan edges doubled around everything

works.t: Obinna Diallo, a man who walks the block during the countdown because he cannot watch
works.s: Obinna walks the block during the countdown because watching is worse. A countdown on a blank glowing screen behind him

works.t: Denise Pinkney, a woman who shoots long exposures from a DUMBO rooftop
works.s: Denise shoots long exposures from a DUMBO rooftop. A camera held under a coat in the rain on the stairs

works.t: Danuta Horvat, a woman who photographs from a moving car window across the bridge
works.s: Danuta photographs from a moving car window across the bridge. A big inkjet printing one physical of the blur

works.t: Priya Pillai, a woman who photographs garbage night on the East Village sidewalk as source
works.s: Garbage night on the East Village sidewalk is Priya's source material. Bags stacked like a monument until the truck

works.t: Franco Ferrante, a man who borrowed against a piece and is now watching the price
works.s: Franco borrowed against a piece and is watching the price. A barber cape and a phone held under it

works.t: Sarala Ackerman, a collector who spends a fixed share of every sale on other artists
works.s: Sarala spends a fixed share of every sale on other artists. A hardware wallet in a velvet box, the tithe automatic

works.t: Danuta Stanescu, a woman who shoots long exposures from a DUMBO rooftop
works.s: Danuta shoots long exposures from a DUMBO rooftop. A closet of labelled hard drives holds every night

works.t: Yasmin Osmani, a collector who spends a fixed share of every sale on other artists
works.s: Yasmin spends a fixed share of every sale on other artists. A contract on a phone beside an untouched drink

works.t: Zainab Narayanan, a person who logs on at the same time every night out of habit
works.s: Zainab logs on at the same time every night out of habit. One empty chair pulled up beside her, also habit

works.t: Naftali Zilberman, a man refreshing in a stairwell at work
works.s: Naftali refreshes in a stairwell at work. A rooftop speaker and a string of lights waiting for the night

works.t: The Man Who Says the Points Farming Sucked the Oxygen Out, for BatSoupYum
works.s: The points farming sucked the oxygen out of the room. A one way bridge between two islands with no span back

works.t: The Woman Who Ran the Launch Party Anyway
works.s: She ran the launch party anyway and carried the room's mood as her job. A rooftop, a folding table of drinks, a speaker

works.t: Consuelo Castellanos, a technician who runs the plotters for everybody
works.s: Consuelo runs the plotters for everybody. A laser level and a pencil behind the ear for the show

works.t: Malka Zilberman, a person who watches the chart to avoid thinking about something else
works.s: Malka watches the chart to avoid thinking about something else. A coffee gone cold hours ago, the something else

works.t: Dae-ho Chow, a man who has not told anybody how much
works.s: Dae-ho has not told anybody how much. A stoop at dawn and an unsent message with the number

works.t: Zev Silverstein, a man who shoots film and scans it the same night
works.s: Zev shoots film and scans it the same night. A camera held under a coat in the rain, then the scanner

works.t: The Woman Who Answers Every Ticket
works.s: She answers every ticket, some of them from a work bathroom stall. A queue that never empties

f2_east.name: The Twenty Houses and The Ten Rooms
f2_east.why: Eras XVI and XVII: a thousand houses and five hundred rooms, the census at its widest.

works.t: Sekou Sanogo, a bridge toll operator in a booth the size of a phone box
works.s: He took the better title and lost the better hours. A radio desk at three, one microphone, an aisle of glowing shelves

works.t: Boruch Weiss, a doorman who stamped the hands of a generation on the Bowery
works.s: Stamping hands under a canopy is a small job with long consequences. Rain on the Bowery, a queue that does not shrink, ink on a wrist

works.t: Petronella Dorsainvil, a woman who answers a crisis line from two to eight
works.s: Generous past the point of sense, six hours a night, no exceptions. A lit booth, no headlights in either direction, a receiver warm against her ear

works.t: Yangzom Gurung, a dispatcher who runs a whole borough by radio
works.s: Runs a borough by radio and has never written any of it down. Sunrise exactly, a booth on a bridge, a river going from grey to gold

works.t: Everton Toussaint, a night security guard doing a route he could walk asleep
works.s: Quiet fury, immaculate manners, and a wage that matches neither. A lantern in a tunnel, a humming rail, a headlight not yet around the curve

works.t: Ming-hua Baek, a marine contractor raising a bulkhead by hand
works.s: He raises other people's edges and nobody has raised his. A glowing panel says rain, and the crew is already in the truck

works.t: Min-seo Chow, a fuel truck driver refuelling a sleeping city
works.s: Strangers get the warmth and the family gets the caution. Sleeping through the loudest hours behind shut curtains and one turning fan

works.t: Ephraim Blum, a cab driver eating alone at a counter at two
works.s: One uninterrupted hour is the whole of his ambition. A griddle nineteen years warm, a coat still on, and a bare bulb

works.t: Yasmin Barakat, a woman who has run the amateur night for thirty years
works.s: Thirty years of amateur nights, and she has never had an hour alone. A box office cage pulled halfway down, a stamp pad, a long queue

works.t: Chinelo Balogun, a bodega owner with sixteen cameras and one blind corner
works.s: Running a bodega means owning sixteen cameras and trusting exactly none. From the window at four she watches the man watching her door

works.t: Damion Achille, a bartender at a hotel bar with a mural everybody photographs
works.s: Somebody has locked this door every night since 1854 and tonight it is him. An untuned piano against the wall, a photographed mural, a smooth old key

works.t: The Rider Who Knows the City Better Than Any Map
works.s: Boubacar has crossed this bridge four hundred times and never once been hired. Every route he ever rode burns behind him as one long line

works.t: The Twenty Two Year Old Doing the Hardest Job in the City
works.s: Twenty two years old and better at this than people twice her age. Scrubs a size too big, a hair tie on her wrist, a laugh

works.t: Priya Raghunathan, a woman who reads the ticket numbers out over the noise
works.s: Reading numbers over that noise is a voice job and a nerve job. Reaching into a barrel to the elbow, brine to the wrist, no gloves

works.t: Radmila Kaczmarek, a transit worker watching four hundred platform feeds
works.s: Four hundred platforms and she is looking for one specific person. Another camera goes up on a facade already covered by nine lenses

works.t: Nadia Wierzbicki, a girl who is the only one in her grade without one
works.s: Only kid in the grade without one, and she is not apologizing. In the schoolyard she runs the transaction and everybody waits their turn

works.t: Kavitha Mirza, a woman with a churro cart on a subway platform watching for the badge
works.s: She knows the work completely and almost nothing else about her own life. A platform, a churro cart, one eye down the tunnel for the badge

works.t: Akiko Xu, a subway track worker in a tunnel with a lantern
works.s: Ask her how she is doing and watch the whole night change. A lantern below the platform, a thermos with opinions, keys back on a hook

works.t: Hoda Khalil, a woman with a churro cart on a subway platform watching for the badge
works.s: Everyone needs her at noon and nobody calls her at night. An office block emptying, a churro cart, a visor, a folded paper napkin

works.t: Pema Sarmiento, a woman with a churro cart on a subway platform watching for the badge
works.s: Ask her Monday and she says yes, then resents it by Thursday. A landmark, tourists three deep, a steam tray, two squeeze bottles

works.t: Cristeta Bhutia, a woman at a Coney Island boardwalk stand from 1916
works.s: Everything she knows lives in her hands and nowhere on paper. A platform, a cart, one eye on the badge coming down the stairs

works.t: Rosalba Zambrano, a bridge painter who never finishes because it starts again
works.s: A bridge is never finished, which is either a job or a sentence. A framed union card, a cab above the skyline, and no day off in sight

works.t: The Nurse on Her Third Day
works.s: Eleven people bought the ticket, so the report home is always good. Third day, four bags, a key that will not turn, one eye flower in the window

works.t: Booker Pinkney, a bridge painter who watches the tide all day
works.s: Nobody watches the harbour more hours a day than a bridge painter. At dusk he wades a street of mirrored sky and floating eye flowers

works.t: Feng Baek, a bridge toll operator in a booth the size of a phone box
works.s: Finishing takes longer than the block will stay the same. Home at sunrise, coat still on, standing in a doorway over a sleeping wife

works.t: Rocco Feeney, a bartender at a Village room that has been a refuge since 1864
works.s: Being needed all night is not the same as being called back. High tide on the wainscot, dusty wishbones, and a bar older than the Bridge

works.t: Marvin Bridges, a bridge toll operator in a booth the size of a phone box
works.s: His pride is load bearing, so nobody has ever tried to remove it. Three in the morning, an aisle of glowing packages, a jacket stiff as cardboard

works.t: Shabana Subramanian, a woman at a Coney Island boardwalk stand from 1916
works.s: Trust takes her a year and then it never comes back off. A truck window, a cone for a small child, twelve hours on her feet

works.t: Lech Kovalenko, a cab driver eating alone at a counter at two
works.s: Twelve hours behind the wheel, and not one conversation in them. A booth at three, a textbook, and a wok flame climbing behind the pass

works.t: Peg Marchetti, a subway track worker in a tunnel with a lantern
works.s: Believed the first time is the whole request, and it never happens. Keys back on a hook, a lantern hung up, a dark booth

works.t: Yosuke Tran-Wu, an electrician reading a panel like a diary
works.s: Most competent on the crew is a title that costs him every weekend. A cab above the whole skyline, alone, a helmet carrying somebody else's name

works.t: Damaris Nunez-Paz, a woman driving a soft serve truck that plays eight bars forever
works.s: Forgiveness comes so fast from her that people mistake it for indifference. Midnight rain, a cart broken down, a fruit cup left for the night man

works.t: Danuta Ilic, a woman selling flowers outside a subway entrance
works.s: She keeps a running tally and swears to everyone that she does not. Dusk, a bright window, a paper tray, a lifetime of unsigned receipts

works.t: Desmond Blackman, a doorman who stamped the hands of a generation on the Bowery
works.s: A second at the door is the whole audition, and he knows it. A wedge shaped basement below, a stamp pad, a queue in the rain

works.t: Nikki Starks, a woman who answers a crisis line from two to eight
works.s: Six hours a night she is the only voice somebody hears. A depot before dawn, rows of buses, a coffee balanced on a dash

works.t: Farid Jarrah, a hotel night auditor who sees the city's whole personality
works.s: Between two and five a hotel lobby shows you the whole city. A train home crowded with people going to work, and one sleeping man

works.t: Layal Karimi, a night court clerk
works.s: Court runs until three and she has never taken the day off. Blank glowing shelves, an aisle to herself, keys going back on a hook

works.t: Odessa Baptiste, a bartender at an Union Square room with a hundred year old urinal
works.s: Union Square keeps a room whose plumbing is older than the subway. A small stove in the middle of the floor, a bar older than the block

works.t: Halyna Adamczyk, a bakery night shift starting at one
works.s: Asking for help arrives disguised as doing somebody else a favour. A bathroom sink at the end of the shift, flour still in the seams

works.t: Lhakpa Villanueva-Cruz, a ghost kitchen line cook running four brands off one stove
works.s: Leaving is the answer and everybody knows it except the one leaving. Top of the bridge at two, one foot down, both boroughs in view

works.t: Farhan Krishnamurthy, a hotel night auditor who sees the city's whole personality
works.s: Certain about the ledger and lost about everything else, he balances both. A radio desk at four, a live microphone, a borough of insomniacs

works.t: Abena Mensah, a subway track worker in a tunnel with a lantern
works.s: Pride costs her things that pride should not cost anybody. A crisis line at four, the right words, one held telephone

works.t: Esti Katzenberg, a transit worker watching four hundred platform feeds
works.s: Four hundred platforms on one wall, and she watches all of them. At dusk the infrared comes on and every platform turns to silver

works.t: Dae-ho Nakamura, a night security guard doing a route he could walk asleep
works.s: Politeness is the container and the fury is what it holds. A crisis line at four, glowing shelves, a lukewarm cup of coffee

works.t: Desmond Saint-Fleur, a locksmith for the whole subway system
works.s: Every gate in the system answers to keys he carries in one pocket. Dawn at height, the mask lifted, a thermos cooling on a girder

works.t: Mendel Rubinstein, a carpenter framing a room he will never see finished
works.s: He frames rooms he will never stand in once they are done. A tool belt worn smooth, a cab above the skyline, one long shift

works.t: Icilda Hyacinth, a car service driver watching charts between fares
works.s: Twelve hours of fares and the phone still gets the last word. A ring of faces lit from below, and one platform minute with her eyes on the tunnel

works.t: Bernadette Halloran, a teenager at her first show at the front barrier
works.s: She wants a receipt for the night that rearranged her whole life. Rain under a narrow canopy, an ink stamp drying on the back of a hand

works.t: The Man in the Bridge Booth
works.s: Four seconds of conversation per car, and the cars have stopped coming. Ruben holds out a hand at three in the morning to an empty bridge

works.t: Bayarmaa Lama, a woman who sells tamales on a platform and watches for the badge
works.s: Selling tamales on a platform means watching the stairs more than the customers. Back table after close, counting the night into stacks of small bills

f2_north.name: The City That Answers Back
f2_north.why: Era XV. The city starts talking.

works.t: The Subway Dancer Who Takes No Money
works.s: He works the whole car and gives every dollar back. The L train, a businessman refused three times and unexpectedly moved

works.t: The Bridge Cable That Sings the Weather
works.s: One note for every kind of weather coming, and he has not been wrong since. Nineteen years reading the main cable, and a ferry captain who will explain it to nobody
A deposit withheld in 1994 came back with thirty years of interest. Bay Ridge, nobody delivered it, a woman on her steps doing the arithmetic

works.t: The Bridge Painter Who Never Finishes
works.s: Thirty one years on one bridge and he starts again at the far end. He prefers it this way now, a job with no last coat

works.t: The Doorman Who Guards the Hour
works.s: He holds the door on the exact hour between night and morning. Central Park West, and a young woman turned away twice is coming up the block again

works.t: The Opera Singer Above the Deli
works.s: A whole street has arranged its day around her scales. Carroll Gardens, second floor, the deli man below with his slicer stopped

works.t: The One Who Went and Came Back
works.s: Nine years over there, and he has just come back across the water. Everything is different and he is fine, and his sister is running down the Bay Ridge pier
Older constellations sit at the bottom of a Grand Concourse pothole. Asphalt every spring, open again every autumn, and a block that has stopped calling it in
A draft horse pulls a delivery cart up Ninth Avenue and traffic yields. The driver inherited the route from her grandmother

works.t: The Wedding Dress Rebuilt Three Times
works.s: One gown, three brides, fifty years of the same seamstress. Bensonhurst, a girl on the box, two earlier fittings standing in the mirror

works.t: The Subway Car With Nobody On It
works.s: A lit empty car runs the whole system every night, stopping properly. Three in the morning, a platform, and she has decided to get on

works.t: The Taxi That Only Runs at Four
works.s: Between four and five a cab takes you to the address you meant. A woman in the back has just given one she has not said aloud in eleven years

works.t: The Subway Surfer Who Was Never in Danger
works.s: A train has decided it likes him, so it holds him on. A Queens elevated, passengers watching through the glass and staying completely calm

works.t: The Woman Who Feeds the Trains
works.s: She feeds the parked R trains from a bucket and they settle. A Coney Island yard at four, and the new hire watches a subway car lower onto its springs

works.t: The Subway Platform That Holds a Note
works.s: A tiled arch holds any note sung into it for eleven minutes. A Bronx platform, a shy teenager singing, a crowd standing inside the sound
Grates along Lexington tuned themselves and every passing train plays a chord. Four years of a busker learning the harmony, and tonight a rush hour crowd stops dead

works.t: The Whole City Humming at Once
works.s: For eleven seconds every engine and voice in New York lands on one note. The Manhattan Bridge, a woman walking her dog, eye flowers opening along the span
She is the one who was asked, and she is about to answer. An ordinary corner at dawn, the whole era behind her, a blue eye on her wrist

works.t: The Subway Car That Runs on the Old Route
works.s: This train follows a 1924 alignment through tunnels that no longer connect. Somehow the arrival is correct, and the conductor is the only witness
That map is a root system, growing new lines toward wherever people are lonely. A girl is watching a branch reach her block in real time

works.t: The Subway Station That Reopened Itself
works.s: City Hall loop is back in service for anyone who truly needs it. Chandeliers lit, tile gleaming, and one midnight rider inside the wrong century

works.t: The Bodega Awning That Shelters Exactly Enough
works.s: An awning extends to exactly the number of people waiting out the rain. Nostrand Avenue, most of a block covered tonight, and an owner who has stopped pretending not to notice

works.t: The Stoop Where the Whole Family Waits
works.s: Four generations on one stoop, all of them watching the corner. Crown Heights at seven, and the car has just turned it

works.t: The Bodega That Sells the Thing You Lost
works.s: One shelf behind the counter holds whatever you lost most recently. A Brooklyn corner store, and a man being handed keys he lost in 2004

works.t: The Bloom in the Subway Vent
works.s: Something enormous came up through the Lexington grate on nothing. The morning crowd started going around it instead of through

works.t: The Graffiti That Came Back Up
works.s: A 1981 whole car surfaced through the paint as pure colour. The writer is sixty now and standing on the platform as it pulls in

works.t: The Puerto Rican Day Crowd on Fifth
works.s: Flags the whole length of Fifth, and the sound of it. A grandmother in the crowd watching her granddaughter go past in the parade

works.t: The Wedding on the Courthouse Steps
works.s: Married by the city, eleven relatives, one deli bouquet. The courthouse steps in the sun, and a stranger stopping to clap
Every debt on the block lives in his head and nowhere else. Washington Heights, two years carried, a man's money waved off the counter

works.t: The Last Box Out of the Old Place
works.s: Twenty six years fit into the box he is carrying down. A Bay Ridge stoop, one step, a man looking back up at the window
One eye flower blooming in late december against all botany, frost on its petals and its iris calm. A passerby stops to stand guard without knowing why

On a Chinatown rooftop the crowned Squab signs the Peace of the Rooftops beside the tiny crowned rat, one wing print and one paw print pressed in petal ink. Both courts cheer, and the bagel rights hold
The rat king and pigeon queen centered, the basket dog, the deli twins, the peacock, the turtles and the hot duck arranged in a park meadow. The school photo nobody could schedule
Under a Delancey grate a tiny rat receives the bent bottle cap crown while the court presents a bouquet of fallen eye flower petals. The juice box crown retires with full honors
At four in the morning New York falls asleep at once and dreams itself. One eye flower opening at the center of the island, bedrock to rooftop in a single cutaway

Flower Moon night, the one night every eye flower in the city opens at once, eight million faces on rooftops and fire escapes and stoops all looking up together. From above, the streets form one enormous opening iris, and the city finally sees itself seeing
May's moon rises and every eye flower in the city opens at once to look up. One night a year the census takes itself
On his one day off the delivery rider sits still in the park while the city brings him things. A friend with coffee, a kid returning his dropped glove, the e-bike garlanded with one eye flower
Counter space got settled between a cat and a deli slicer without a word. A gold quiet store, a guard blade and two green eyes minding their own business
School doors detonating borough wide, bodega candy futures spiking. Crossing guards conducting the day's great migration home
Iridescent on a bridge cable throne, feathers catching light like an oil slick crown. Squabs and sparrows in attendance, both kingdoms surveyed
The rat king and pigeon queen honeymooning by trash barge gondola under the bridges, fireflies as escorts. Both courts wave from the pilings
She spent a life looking and a block finally looked back. A Brooklyn rooftop at blue hour, every eye flower turned toward one woman with a notebook

Under the great clock where they first looked twice, the whole love thread assembled, from the Missed Connection to the Same Booth. The mismatched mugs were the toast, and every eye flower in the station opened at once
Pigeons licensed themselves as guides for nervous first time flyers. Formation flying around wobbling commuters, gentle herding off the bridge cables, payment in bagel futures
The fisheye holds the entire block in one silver eye. Every aisle, the cat, the counter, a kid waving at himself curved small
We are happy to serve you, and it means it. Blue and gold on a bodega counter at dawn, steam rising like a hymn
The machines ran all night and produced one drawing of the fire escape. Taped to the window at dawn, pencil lines, the light coming through
The panorama model dances inside a wreath of bridge cables, the rat king, the pigeon queen, the angel and the collector holding the corners. Everything in its place, and turning
Two identical bodega cats hold the counter in mirrored poses and nobody in nine years knows which is which. The owner insists there has only ever been one cat, and the mirror behind them is empty

works.t: The Pigeon Queen Lands on a Crane
works.s: Two monarchs surveyed the borough and neither of them spoke. A crane boom above the rooftops, sunrise behind, feathers and lattice holding still
For once the screen understood the assignment and went dark. A passenger crying over the bridge, cables strobing past the black glass
At sunset the layer misaligns and doubles everything in red and cyan. A pigeon keeper reads the fringe like weather, and tonight the borough separates gently from itself
She folds the tunnel and puts Far Rockaway four minutes from Inwood. Only the last train, only for people who have been up too long, and the authority has no idea
He hands her back before the mother finishes turning around. A Bronx stoop rail, a slipped toddler, two arms already there
After the plows pass, the corner snow mountain crowns its king with a hockey stick planted at the summit. His mitten rises like a scepter over everything the streetlight touches
She runs the block from a stool behind the counter. The throne, the neighborhood mother, the eye that misses nothing
A taxi slowed down rather than call it imagination. Four in the morning on a Bronx bridge, headlights, something tawny crossing
The sweeper truck and the Trash Mountain meet at dawn like two generals. The brushes pause, the Mountain yields one lane with dignity
Snowfall makes the Trash Mountain regal, bags dusted white like ermine. Icicle chandeliers on its crown, rats in tiny scarves holding court in its lee
The bees, the monarchs and the kestrel move through the city in one unlikely procession, the eye flowers turning to follow. The pollen route glows gold behind them
One gray January morning a bodega owner erases a regular's winter tab and writes paid in pencil. The regular is never told, and the paperwhite by the lottery machine blooms anyway

boro_staten.name: Staten Island
boro_staten.why: Staten Island, on the atrium wall.

works.s: A retired keeper finds an eye flower budding at the focus of the museum's great Fresnel lens, and the glass wakes to throw one slow beam across the room. The lights are in on it now
She lays out the kit at ten and sleeps none of it. A Staten Island hotel bed, a bib already pinned, the bridge in the window
The night crew fills the monster pothole under work lights, steam rising off fresh blacktop like a healed wound. The cone that sank is retrieved and saluted, the patch smoothed like icing
The lights come on at dusk in one strand across the Narrows, and a Bay Ridge grandmother announces the harbor is wearing its necklace again. Dinner steams behind her, untouched

f3_west.name: Places
f3_west.why: The Places family: the city as the sitter.

works.s: Two shifts trade places at the rail without trading a word. Night going home, day coming in, the harbor between them
Print found a way to reach the one reader it was losing. Subway entrance, pages fanning like wings, a blind commuter standing still in the rush
A warehouse roof greenhouse glows like a docked ship over Greenpoint at dusk while the grower waters in headphones. Commuters look up at the light without knowing why, which is how lighthouses work
She strides up the avenues and the magnolias detonate behind her. Even the scaffolding blooms, the whole city's coat unbuttoning at her pace
An etched mirror kept every face that ever checked itself there. Tonight ninety years of nervous women assemble in the glass to counsel a bride hiding from her reception

works.t: The Rent Party of the Whole City
works.s: To celebrate, the city throws itself a rent party in the old style. Every stoop a stage, the buried streams for ice, the old reliquary ball for the light

works.t: Piotr Wierzbicki, a rain garden crew lead planting for a hundred year storm
works.s: Planting for a storm that arrives every four years is optimism with a shovel. At dusk he wades a street that reflects the whole sky
Backward since 1913, the constellations quietly turned the right way at four. Grand Central, one commuter off a Bellevue night shift, saying finally out loud to an empty concourse
Scaffolding is one continuous forest and Canal Street is its old growth. Standing since 1991, pipes gone bark brown, a bough lowered to meet a grandson's hand
Neon and daylight meet in the middle of the block. Chinatown at dawn, the arcade spilling magenta down the sidewalk, a street sweeper pausing in the seam

works.t: The Harbor Brings the Weather Inside
works.s: Giants carry the harbor's best morning up the avenues in cupped hands. Salt light and gull sound poured over Fordham and Flushing, the whole city oceanfront for an hour
The ancient bedrock surfaces through the park lawn like a whale back, mica glinting like a buried galaxy. The skyline stands exactly where the old stone is strong enough to hold it

works.t: The Chain Link That Blooms Where It Is Missed
works.s: Blossom appears only where hands press the fence to look through. A shuttered Bronx ballfield, eight solid feet of it, and bare wire everywhere else
After hours the glass hall makes its own desert dusk. A night engineer eating his sandwich in the sunset of a country he left

works.t: The Footings of the Old Hotel
works.s: A demolished hotel's footings still hold their posts under a parking lot. At midnight a ghost lobby assembles knee high, its dancers the size of sparrows

works.t: Salma Mansour, a carver at a chophouse where the mutton chop has not changed since 1885
works.s: Somebody younger should learn the cut, and nobody has asked yet. A cold locker, hanging sides of beef, and a chop that predates the subway

works.t: The Fashion of the Waking Year
works.s: Garment district cuts the year's look in a single night out of tank light. Seventh Avenue at dawn, cloth of bridge chord and mirror rain, the invisible client walking finale
Twenty Eighth Street turns into a jungle for four hours daily. A bruised bunch handed over free, one eye flower nobody clocks
In the convex security mirror the counter cat is a monarch in ermine. A throne of stacked cans, the homage of reflected mice, and a chin scratch accepted as tribute
Volume is a form of manners in Bay Ridge. The rooftop speaker carries the call exactly to the last listener, then stops at the bridge

works.t: The Gown Sewn From the Skyline
works.s: On the coldest fashion week night the district cuts a gown from the city itself. River silk hemmed, bridge cable boning, tower lights for buttons, the audience rising floor by floor
The deli twins, the crossing guard, the super, the block mom, all hung in gold frames. The subjects attend opening night pointing at each other, the walls finally honest about who art is for
It lifted the arm for a family that was not coming back. Bridge approach at sunset, a moving truck, the skyline filling the rearview mirror
All day the city introduces itself to itself in the open street. Cast iron ghosts meeting harbor giants, the rat queen presented, New Yorkers threading through, late for lunch
Climbers chalk up on the park's great boulder at dusk, crash pads like lily pads below. A glacier's gift moonlighting as the city's smallest mountain
Coney Island's retired tower lit like a crown at night, light rings climbing the lattice. The parachutes are gone, the drifting feeling never left
Strangers who missed the same train built a school of philosophy on the yellow strip. Trains skip the station gently when the argument is good, proceedings kept in tile echo
One night a year the modern rails remember steam. A ghost plume over the Harlem River and a whistle from eighteen ninety, bridge tenders saluting
Ferns and eye flowers live on the flicker of feet crossing the grate above. A retired horticulturist waters at dawn, the platform below standing in green shadow

works.t: The Penthouse That Kept the Old Roof
works.s: Inside a new crown stands the tar paper roof of the walk up that came first. Clothesline, folding chair, pigeon coop, and the developer born there keeping birds at seven hundred feet

works.t: The Night the City Looked Up
works.s: Ten thousand stone faces turned at once toward one light over the harbor. A sound like a mountain clearing its throat, and every pedestrian below looked up with them
Express and local run side by side, and your reflection is your other life. Eleven stations window to window, long enough to look, to nod, and sometimes to forgive yourself
One plank lifted and returned a ring lost in nineteen seventy four. Coney Island, wood grain, the parachute jump standing behind it all
Dumbo knows exactly what the bridge does to that street. Cobblestones, a wedding party sprinting between trains, an arch holding the shot
A night rain fell that polished instead of rusting. The whole district coming up like silver, a doorman under his portico seeing himself multiplied down five blocks
A hover lane cone, a light thread, one bodega coffee cup, enshrined as relics. The last gallery is a window onto the living street labeled ongoing
They burst from the marriage bureau into confetti thrown by strangers, bodega roses for a bouquet. The getaway car is a granny cart and the marriage will last
Her toll is one sandwich crust and one piece of news from above. No rat crosses a live rail before a train, and every dropped phone comes back
The red cabin sails over the East River at dusk beside the bridge. Commuters and tourists share the same gasp, which happens nowhere else
Farmers once walked their cows to Brooklyn here at low tide. A ferry captain tips his cap to the ankle deep ghost herd of 1780, myth and tide sharing a lane
From six to seven the bodega aisle runs as a runway. The cat judges from the counter, and a nurse off a double gets the lane
On the night the hundred year storm arrives the harbor stands up. Giants linked arm to arm from the Narrows to Hell Gate, eight million windows burning behind them till morning
Justice and Commerce climb down at night for the cases the day court missed. A stolen parking spot, a borrowed ladder never returned, rulings delivered from the courthouse steps

works.t: The Sunken Subway Car Reef Choir
works.s: Subway cars sunk offshore as reef kept their voices. Chimes and closing doors coming in on the surf at Rockaway, the ocean running the old announcements as whale song
Every hour the Brooklyn Bridge ever carried is crossing it right now. Strollers from eighteen eighty three beside hover joggers, cables humming a chord a hundred forty years wide
The loud younger sibling, carrying trains in its teeth beside its famous elder. Blue paint and unshakable confidence
Her first solo night in the lamp room and she mixes her mother's green. Every crown in midtown changes to match, a skyline closing ranks around one lamp room

An easement nobody repealed gives the wire walkers the cables one night a year. Grandmothers spotting granddaughters by lantern light, and the bridge stilling every vibration for the safest impossible walk
The wonder wheel spills its light toward the boardwalk chess of Brighton Beach. Winter swimmers steam in the surf while piroshki and cotton candy share the wind
A night baker feels the deep city turn over before anybody else does. Flour shivering into patterns, a doubled batch, and a line down Arthur Avenue for something with no name

f3_east.name: Design and Builders
f3_east.why: The people who drew it and the people who built it.

works.s: Every line reordered itself into a flower and stayed that way. A lost tourist and a lifelong rider shoulder to shoulder, every station dot an iris
The tiles rearrange themselves into vines a century after the craftsman set them. His hands still visible in ghost form, the station name blooming
A small grandmother calmly closes the jaws of the subway doors with one gentle hand. Force yielding to grace, infinite patience over a flowered hat
Two million people in the square watching one number get ready to roll over. Backstage, a lone technician and the Y2K monitors, the whole century leaning forward
Groceries, lotto, hot food, cold beer, six fonts, zero lies. The yellow awning glows at night like a marquee for everything you need at 2am
Bolted beside the stoop since the 1840s, the mud of two centuries wiped into memory. A modern sneaker uses it correctly and a top hat's ghost nods, small iron outliving empires
The bucket roses close into buds each dawn to be sold fresh twice. On the third day they quit commerce and distribute themselves to every mailbox on the block

works.t: Zahra Chalabi, a bridge painter who never finishes because it starts again
works.s: Painting a bridge ends where it started, forever, by design. A bridge that starts again the day it ends, and one perfect joint

works.t: Efua Balogun, a chef in the dining room that won everything last year
works.s: She is the strong one because nobody else volunteered for it. Flame up in a dark room, sleeves pushed back, an unopened door
Old 42nd Street at full neon sleaze, grindhouse marquees stacked three deep. Popcorn and hustle and a saxophone somewhere, every sign buzzing a different pink

works.t: The Therapist Above the Nail Salon
works.s: Room size tracks exactly how safe the client feels. Flushing, above the nail salon, and today the office is a cathedral

works.t: The Optometrist Who Corrects for Beauty
works.s: Lenses ground here correct for what is good about where you live. Bay Ridge, an old man in a trial pair turning toward the window

works.t: Nechama Lieberman, a roofer in August with tar and no shade
works.s: Being believed the first time would save about four hours a week. An open panel of a hundred wires, and a skyline of lit windows
She refuses about half the sales, which is why the table is trusted. A remote that pauses one argument, a charger that runs on thanks, a speaker that plays what the room needs

works.t: The Stoop Speaker of Perfect Volume
works.s: Every listener hears it at exactly the volume they need. Loud for the dancing, inaudible to the baby upstairs, correct for the old man pretending not to listen
Running half a second behind, the layer makes every delivery arrive twice. She hands the ghost bag to the kid at the door while the real one climbs the stairs, still hot
Look at the mosaic long enough and the corner goes back a century. Tesserae shifting on a station wall, a platform crowd flowing past without noticing
A rooftop water tower struck by summer lightning, staves flying like cards. The crown of water becomes rain, and the gardens below drink the sudden change
The neon runs like wet paint down the night glass. One clear drop holds the whole skyline sharp inside it
Open on a stoop at night, the grease bloom like a rose window, steam rising in gold ribbons. The little plastic table stands guard, as it was born to do
At dawn on a rooftop the eye flowers bloom off the wet canvas into the real skyline. Every character faintly visible in the clouds, one blue evil eye signed into the corner
The wonder wheel turning with fates in its swinging cars, rat king rising as landlord descends. The boardwalk sphinx counts the revolutions from the pier
The modernist map lifts its route lines off the paper into neon ribbons. Beautiful, legendary, and famously never quite where the streets are
He steps off the bus with one suitcase and total faith, a bodega cat at his heels. The skyline is the cliff he cannot see, and he will survive it
The community garden queen on a milk crate throne, tomatoes and eye flowers at full yield. She willed this lot green and it obeyed
One slice and one subway token in perfect equilibrium on a balance scale above the skyline. Economists and counter guys nodding together
A subway passage blooms with thousands of bright squares, strangers answering strangers between trains. One commuter reads three, adds one, and walks out lighter
1967, the first air conditioned subway car arrives like a miracle on rails. Platforms let the hot trains pass and wait for the cold one

Every name in the census on one impossible stage, the rat king beside the angel, the countdown clock beside the crossing guard, the eight million in the seats. The seventh chapter takes its bow, and the city applauds itself for once

works.t: The Subway Car With No Layer
works.s: One car on the D runs with nothing blooming in the air. Riders sprint the platform for it, and inside there is paper, a window, and occasional conversation
Presented on deli paper like a crown jewel, seeds orbiting like a galaxy. Sesame, poppy, garlic: everything means everything
Bent glass veins of pink and blue feeding every night corner. The pulse made visible, the hum that refuses to sleep
1884, and Barnum walks twenty one elephants across the new bridge to prove it safe. The lead one pauses mid span to survey the harbor like a queen
An old couple flagged down the last checker cab in 1999 like it was 1965. Jump seats folded one final time, the great yellow whale gliding to the museum
Brass with a Y cutout, coin of a lost empire, floating above the turnstile altar. Ask anyone who carried one, it still spends
An ad quit advertising and became a paper flower instead. Creases folding down into a sleeping woman's lap, an empty orange car
Built for the worst night, it finally moved on an ordinary one. Lower East Side iron curling down for a stranded cat, the whole block in the windows
They drafted his coat from the shape of his whole route. Forty years of a subway line pinned to a wall, then cut and stitched into a coat
The missed connection pair on facing platforms, the angel of the waters rising between the tracks above them. Two trains arriving as one choice
A film set bodega built overnight, so perfect the neighbors try to shop there. Prop oranges refused to a confused regular, the cat auditioning itself into the movie
Streetwear collaborated with the subway and the clerks refused to change out of it. Transit workwear, roundel hang tags, a launch held on a working platform
In a taxi's back seat a designer sketches three small letters and a heart on an envelope scrap. The city's whole logo born between two red lights, the cabbie unaware he is driving history
Sticks blurring over upturned buckets on the platform, the rhythm rising in arcs of color. A whole crowd forgets its train, which is the highest honor we give
Hard hat under his arm like a crown at rest, every tower behind him one of his. The puddle at his feet wears the whole skyline
A row of them glowing in the bodega cooler like stained glass, every neon color, condensation like jewels. One small hand reaches in, twenty five cents from paradise
The machine has told Coney Island's fortune for a hundred seasons. This time the card slides out blank and glowing, and the mystic just watches
Forty years of fares under the swinging beads, an evil eye charm and a small flag sharing the mirror stem. The dashboard's quiet altar keeping every ride safe
A collar translates, and it turns out the cat has plenty to say. Consulted on hiring now, correct most of the time, and paid in a considerably better chair
One counter runs down the middle of two versions of the same store. Rendered customers on one hand, a chopped cheese on the other, equal respect, and a real cat asleep in the seam
A crane operator keeps one orchid in the cab four hundred feet over Tenth Avenue and waters it from a thermos cap at lunch. Highest garden in the city, one plant, perfect attendance

f3_north.name: The Sets
f3_north.why: One piece from each of the biggest sets, hung together so the series read as series.

works.s: She built a rig that watches the watchers and found out it is boring. Hours of a cat, a leaf, an old man sitting down, so she started leaving beautiful things in frame

works.t: Nusrat Narayanan, an office cleaner alone on a lit floor at midnight
works.s: Kinder to strangers than to anyone waiting at home, and she knows it. An empty avenue before dawn, a sweeper, one pair of headlights
Under a Queens data hall the dead are kept as footage. A night technician plays clips into the empty aisles so that somebody is watching, which he considers the job

works.t: Leah Teitelbaum, a night companion paid to simply be awake in a house
works.s: Being awake is the entire job, and it is harder than it sounds. Four in the morning, a notebook of times and doses, a strange lamp
One viewer is an audience when he is on a night shift overseas. A warm cluttered kitchen, a grandmother cooking, a phone holding steady

works.t: Sybil Toussaint, a woman who keeps the recipes written on index cards
works.s: Help gets requested only when disguised as a favour to somebody else. A jacket that no longer fits, put on for a Sunday, on a stoop

works.t: Bridget Belsky, a grandmother raising a second generation of grandchildren
works.s: Raising them twice does not come with a second thank you. Watching somebody young get it right, from a doorway, in a rent controlled apartment

works.t: The Woman Who Lost the House
works.s: She was not stupid, which is the part nobody will believe. Bay Ridge to a rented room, one enormous sofa from a bigger life
The largest lens in the city, the one that never closes, closes. One second above Times Square, eight million people feeling the pressure change, one night nurse seeing the lash

works.t: Aaron Landau, a bodega cat's owner who is also everybody's uncle
works.s: Uncle to a whole block and asked by nobody how he is. Seven in the morning, a lease letter in the pocket, the night shift filling the stools
Drones roost now and pigeons hover, and Delancey cannot tell them apart. The man with the seed bag feeds all of it, and the six o'clock flock rises half machine

works.t: The Night the Cameras Looked Away
works.s: Every lens in New York turned to face the harbor and left the city alone. People used the privacy for almost nothing dramatic, sitting closer, saying the thing, crying in public

works.t: Cheryl Devereaux, a fuel truck driver refuelling a sleeping city
works.s: Warm with strangers, guarded with family, and aware it is backwards. A bathroom sink at the end of it, cold water, a face in the mirror

works.t: Esti Blum, a bakery night shift starting at one
works.s: Whoever feeds the block before it wakes is never asked how she is. Seven in the morning, sunglasses on, walking home against a tide of commuters

works.t: Akiko Zhang, a librarian who saved the local files from the dumpster
works.s: A dumpster had the neighbourhood's paperwork in it, so she took it home. Now she carries boxes down a stoop, hunting for a younger pair of hands

works.t: Siobhan Halloran, a dispatcher who runs a whole borough by radio
works.s: Competence became the room she hides in, and the radio never closes. A lit booth at three, no headlights in either direction, a thermos

works.t: Booker Odom, a man who has run the same corner slice shop since 1971
works.s: Arguing about pizza with total seriousness is how this city says hello. Fifty years on one corner, one oven, one price on the board

works.t: Ah-lam Yamashita, a bodega owner with sixteen cameras and one blind corner
works.s: Sixteen cameras and the one thing worth seeing happened in the blind corner. Asked to point at a face on the tape, she looks at the floor

works.t: Bo Jeong, a bridge painter who watches the tide all day
works.s: Two hundred feet up, the tide is the only clock he trusts. From the boat home the skyline sits low against a rising harbour

works.t: Bayarmaa Abdrakhmanov, a night court clerk
works.s: Night court runs on one clerk who knows exactly what is happening. Keys going back on a hook at dawn, a hallway, a locked door

works.t: Miroslav Melnyk, a locksmith for the whole subway system
works.s: Every lock in the subway opens for one man with a ring of keys. A mask lifted, a field of lit windows below, no door with his name

works.t: Shanice Danridge, a bodega owner with sixteen cameras and one blind corner
works.s: Sixteen cameras cover her store and she watches the one blind corner. A housing on the ceiling has opened like a flower above the register

works.t: Rajesh Narayanan, a man who has run the same route since 1979
works.s: Same route since 1979, and everything he knows he keeps to himself. A stoop, a photograph wall, and a whole life hung in one hallway

works.t: Dorje Rai, a boy from Ohio who has told nobody he is terrified
works.s: Ohio thinks he is doing great and he intends to keep it that way. A familiar food found in a deli case, finger tracing a line on the map

f4_west.name: The Mythos and The Deep City
f4_west.why: Eras VI and VII: the Rat King is crowned and the city goes underground.

works.s: A full Christmas tree rides the subway upright between its new family, baptizing the car in pine. Strangers breathe deep and forgive everything, the star riding in a coat pocket like a secret
The tunnel wall opens all at once as the headlights sweep past. Petals turning to follow the light like a crowd at a parade, closing into darkness behind
The exact minute morning sun pours down the subway stairs, commuters ascending into a wall of gold. A daily minor heaven, metrocards glowing in raised hands
Second bottles and homework surrendered, dog walkers on last patrol. The skyline fully lit and slightly overdressed, everything still possible
A quiet regular gets his ten gallon pin at the blood bank, eighty strangers saved on lunch breaks. The pin small as a dime and heavy as a bridge, juice and cookies for the banquet
The city's electricity rides the third rail as a slender figure of light, racing the train. It splits at junctions, delivers power like a paper route, never touched and never stopping
The sea road express bursting from tunnel into Coney sunlight, salt air through the doors at the last stop. A yellow bullet with sand in its shoes
A young man rises in one smooth arc and a tired elder's face travels from fatigue to grace. The whole car warms one degree as the train sings through the tunnel
Hundreds of cyclists receive holy water on handlebars and helmets, wheels raised at the benediction. Ghost bike riders remembered in the litany before the peloton rolls out into spring
The bar erupts at 7am, every nation's jersey pressed against one screen, espresso and pints in the same fists. Geography dissolves in the roar as the block outside answers in car horns
The stolen bar umbrella opens into a private downpour one block later while the sky behind stays dry. Its true owner steps out into sudden sunshine, the books balanced in ninety seconds
Every August she waters the whole floor's plants with a brass can and everyone's spare keys. The ferns lean toward her arrival, a hallway of jungles thriving on trust
A nearly invisible wire encircles the island, checked weekly by one quiet inspector with binoculars. A boundary of faith drawn in fishing line, hidden in plain sky
The long lunch and the eaten desk, chess tables at full clock. The first hooky matinee ticket sold to someone deserving
The new gantry glows over the avenue like a modern city gate, sensors reading the air itself. History charging by the axle
An unsigned love letter dropped in the blue mailbox, addressed only to new york. Years later the dead letter office steams it open and reads it aloud to the shelves
A gown of woven MetroCard silver, a crown of polished bottle cap. She holds court on a velvet subway seat, attendants presenting crumbs of state
Honeybees run the subway map for real, carrying iris pollen between boroughs. Each one trails a thread of light, and eye flowers open where they land
Eye flowers blooming through snow along a fence line, irises open under frost caps. A kid clears snow around each one with a mitten, and winter concedes
Sixty blocks at night to outpace a feeling, the city dispensing therapy in bridge lights and bodega cats. Home tired enough to sleep, lighter by ten blocks
5am in the flower district, armfuls of blooms blinking sleepily as they are wrapped. A hand truck stacked with watching bouquets, a tiny crowned rat supervising
One glowing seed sleeps beneath the subway lines and water tunnels. Roots threading every tunnel like veins, the whole skyline resting on its light
The trash prince comes of age atop rat rock at midnight, climbers' chalk marks as sacred runes. The juice box crown exchanged for a bottle cap one

They exchange vows in the subway car exactly where they met, the conductor officiating over the intercom. Straphangers hold bodega roses as the rings pass hand to hand down the car, arriving perfectly
The rooftop as the block's private riviera, towels on hot tar and a radio between chimneys. Pigeon coops for cabanas, the skyline for an ocean view
One couch split down the middle in two jerseys, the dog in a neutral bandana. Grandma keeps score with terrifying accuracy, bragging rights on the line for a full year
A baby's first subway ride, eyes enormous at the tunnel lights. The whole car softens into a ring around the stroller while the city introduces itself gently
Costumed kids board the subway with baskets of treats in a delivery blitz. A tiny queen esther and a dinosaur handing hamantaschen to a delighted stranger
The block holds its annual mayoral race between three bodega cats, posters bearing only paw prints. The incumbent sleeps on the scale mid debate, democracy purring
The flower district elder teaches one apprentice the eye flower's care, how to meet its gaze and when to look away. The shop's other flowers lean in to eavesdrop
The 1946 plan, an airport on the rooftops a hundred midtown blocks long. Ghost airliners taxi past office windows, the delirious blueprint that almost was
The baker, the nurse, the dispatcher, the cab driver and the tower cat's keeper sharing counter light at 4am. The night shift holding its own communion
Second date, crossing the bridge at dusk, two coffees gone cold from talking. The skyline ignites behind them, a heavy handed but effective wingman
The scenic route over the bridge, with a harbor view it pretends not to show off. The moon rides with it, and neither one brags
The east side's crowded confidant. At night it loops the old City Hall station like a secret bow to its grandmother
A hand lettered poster on the same platform where two trains once erased a question. Phone number tabs flutter like hope, and one is already gone
The same two strangers finally meet on the mezzanine between their platforms, both holding the same poster, both early. The turnstiles applaud softly in clicks while the city pretends it planned this
Ten thousand irises across a warehouse roof, all facing the sunrise in unison. The sigil writer's largest work, signed in one neon line in the corner
One determined man walks a queen mattress eight blocks on his head while the wind turns it into a sail. A doorman and a hot dog vendor rate the technique as he tacks past
Every year at the same AirTrain window where the skyline first appeared, one deli coffee raised to the glass. The city returns the toast with its evening lights
The hinge of everything, yesterday and tomorrow shaking hands on every corner. One baker starting as one dancer finishes, the eye flowers all open at once
The full moon paces the train across the bridge, keeping perfect speed between the cables. Every kid aboard certain it follows only them
Both trains arrive at once with the doors aligned across the platform. Commuters glide between them in a beam of light, one man laughing out loud at his luck
A translucent runner of newspaper scraps and warm air sprints the platform. Thirty seconds ahead of the train, lifting coats, turning every head toward the tunnel
The bodega, the stoop, the hydrant, the block mom's window and the handball wall arranged like a family. One kid walking home from the last day of school, surrounded
A kid's first solo subway trip, standing tall by the door with the instructions memorized. Mom tracking the dot with her heart in her throat, the conductor somehow knowing
Rooftop menorahs glow down the boulevard in a parade of horns and waving kids. The ninth night turns the whole avenue into a moving constellation
The traffic engineer conducts the avenue's green wave like a symphony. Lights cascade up the map in a visible ripple and one grateful cab surfs the whole thing
A patient technician adjusts the small brass gears of hope. Recalibrating two minutes to mean two minutes, the platform not yet ready to believe
The basket dog races the bridge at dawn with a cargo of glowing charms. Protection delivered door to door, one already hung on his own collar

f4_east.name: The Fabric and The Bloom
f4_east.why: Eras VIII and IX: the texture of the place, then the flowers.

works.s: The elevator falls eighteen stories to a platform inside the mountain itself. The bedrock sweats cool and the train arrives like a vein of light through stone
A retired doorman orders two coffees every morning and hands the second to whoever looks like the night was long. The cart man builds that one sweeter
Sunday afternoon turns the stoop into a salon, three generations braiding hair down the steps in a row to laughter and gossip. The youngest holds the beads like crown jewels, because they are
The lunch rush obeys the raised wooden peel and lands exactly where she points. The sauce jars glow behind her like rubies of state

works.t: The Last Petal of the Night
works.s: A sweeper works Broadway at 4:58am, pushing a river of fallen glowing petals toward the dawn and pocketing exactly one. Behind his broom the drift settles into the shape of a sleeping face, and he lets it sleep
Three retired men on a Bay Ridge bench rate every dog that passes, and a dachshund in a raincoat takes full marks. The owner bows on behalf of her athlete
One shining seat on a packed train, and everyone stands. Nobody knows the source, nobody runs the experiment
The Hippodrome elephants walk to work down Sixth Avenue at dawn, trunks holding tails in a patient gray parade. A boy on a stoop forgets his own name
A whole block party runs off one extension cord out of apartment 1B's window, DJ, fans and a bounce house negotiated across it. The tenant of 1B eats free all night, like any utility
Two ropes sing their double dutch rhythm while a girl rocks at the edge counting her doorway in. She lands the entry clean and the whole stoop keeps score in claps

A Delancey Street turnstile grows overnight into a flowering gate and the token booth clerk refuses to file the report, waving riders through the petals. One commuter bows slightly on his way to work, as you do at a gate
Same stoop, same order, one photo a year for nineteen years, grandma holding the center like a keystone. The kids are taller than the door now
A wheatpaste man rolls a show poster onto plywood at 4am in three practiced strokes, brush, sweep, done. Beneath it, a decade of layers curls like tree rings
End of shift, counter wiped to a mirror, his own first cup of the day. Every stool holds the ghost of a good day's regular
A showtime dancer's sneaker passes one inch from a seated rider's nose at full swing and the car inhales together. He lands clean and collects his applause and his dollar
You getting off, asked once at the doors, and the packed car resolves itself like a math problem. Nobody taught anyone the dance
The rooftop hives drew from the elevated line blooms and the frames came up glowing. Hold a jar to the sun and one tiny iris of light looks back
In the Rat Court's tunnel market a tiny crowned rat weighs rose petals on a bottle cap scale for a patient line. The juice box crown prince inspects quality personally
Eye flowers climb the Brooklyn Bridge cables like ivy while a painter on the walkway paints them faster than they climb. His canvas is a tower ahead, and the joggers stop to check the score

A whole subway car quietly minds a sleeping stranger's stop, and the woman across the aisle wakes him one station early. Three riders confirm his transfer in unison, then everyone goes back to ignoring each other
The regular enters, the order begins unbidden, one nod carries the whole contract. The cat approves from the chip rack throne
He knelt where they first looked twice, holding a ring made from a subway token. The commuters stopped mid stride, and for once nobody minded the delay
The last civilian keeper climbs the Coney Island Light one more time at dusk, the boardwalk wheels turning small below. Fifty years of the same grip wore the rail bright
A kid chalks the entire block onto the sidewalk, hydrant, stoops, deli, and the crowd watching him draw. He adds each new arrival until the drawing catches up to now
Packing for a move, a transplant finds the subway map she once studied nightly, creased soft as cloth and unopened in two years. She files it with the letters worth keeping
Wax filled bottle caps and a chalked grid, the summer game of record. The champion cap wears a tiny crown, and the Rat Court considers this correct
The 3am garden car arrives at an empty platform blooming floor to ceiling, doors opening on nobody, a brass watering can strapped by the door. One night cleaner steps in and rides one stop younger
A transplant walks her visiting parents past the deli, the dry cleaner and her fire escape, narrating like she poured the sidewalks herself. Her father is quietly proud in a giant foam crown
An entire train car painted end to end rolled out of the yard at sunrise, 1979. Two kids at the fence with stained hands watched their names cross the bridge in ten foot letters of light
Above, the Squab rides the J train roof, below, the Rat Court parades in step. The commuters in between feel strangely blessed all day
He summits the subway stairs and stops dead at the top to consult the sky. Behind him, humanity compresses into one hot accordion
Zip tied planters appear overnight along a quarter mile of scaffolding pipes, marigolds at eye level, sigil paint still drying on the plywood. Nobody saw anything, and everybody slows under the bloom
Tied outside the deli, he tracks the door with the focus of an air traffic controller, taking updates from every exiting stranger. His tail translates each report into hope
A pigeon has learned the Court Street bakery opens at 6:14 and arrives at 6:13 to pace like a foreman until the bolt turns. The baker denies the friendship and saves the crusts anyway
The barber chair came out onto the stoop for the groom's wedding cut. Half the block supervised from the steps, and the cape caught the wind like a matador
Night shift and day shift cross on the same platform at 6am, scrubs one way and hard hats the other. One nod between strangers holds the whole arrangement up
Friday payday empties the deli flower buckets by seven as the whole neighborhood walks home holding cellophane cones. The florist restocks twice and calls it the holiday the block invented for itself
The survey office map room drawer slides open again and the hand inked city iris has grown a second ring of petals reaching into the outer boroughs. The night archivist lays her ruler down unused
Four degens hold a rooftop funeral for a hard drive holding a wallet nobody can open, one deli carnation on the case. The eulogy quotes the peak balance from memory, moment of silence included
Every cab in the city goes off duty at once, roof lights dimming in waves as arms rise unanswered on every corner. The sacrament is observed daily and hated ecumenically
A woman surfaces from the subway mid block and performs the ancient squint at the light to find uptown. Two seconds, recalibrated, gone, with tourists trailing her like ducklings
Strollers roll past the lawn marys toward Red Hook's harbor cranes. The canal bridge lifts for a barge, and the salt air carries key lime pie

January snow on the Painter's windowsill, and one impossible green bud pushes up through it from the flower box while the mismatched mugs steam on the sill. The garden keeps its promise, and so does he
Locked out in the snow with the warm neon at their backs. One slice rotates alone in the lit case like a lighthouse that cannot help

The bodega's new kitten makes her counter debut riding the register scale while the block files through all afternoon with congratulations. The older cat supervises from the chip rack like a retiring champion
The block papers its poles for a lost cat who is asleep behind the deli register the whole time. The reward gets renegotiated by the cat
The hottest night of the year moves the whole building to the stoop at midnight with lemon ices. Spoons scrape paper cups in the dark while the super ranks every summer worse than this one
The warm metal breath of an arriving express reaches the platform before its headlights do. She lifts her face into it like a doorway of heat, which underground it is
The north shore watches the ferry come and go like a tide. Victorians and spice shops share the harbor view while the tugs nudge the world past
The harbor island's lawn crew files off the morning ferry with municipal dignity. The skyline across the water pretends this is normal, because it is

f4_north.name: The Look, The Waking, The Arrival

works.s: Decades of swallowed coins came back in one bright avalanche. Bronx mezzanine, commuters on their knees gathering silver, an apology the size of a screen
Chrome silverfish swim the tunnels between trains like mercury weather. Good luck if they circle you, better luck if one pauses at your shoe
A paper cup by the register filled to the price of a train home. Night street through the door, a cashier counting once and stopping
She left the booth, which the job does not require. An eighty year old walked to the right platform wearing her coat

works.t: The Bodega TV Plays the Game
works.s: Nobody could switch it off, so nobody tried. Ninth inning, eleven strangers in the chip aisle, the cat asleep across the set
Chrome sparrows run a livery service for the insect rush hour. Ladybugs and bumblebees in cabs of folded wing, dispatch handled from a Union Square lamppost
It skipped the Hudson like a stone and left rings from nineteen twenty. Dawn, a ferry crowd filming from the rail, the Palisades gone pink behind them
Every size came back for exactly four minutes and the servers never explained. A mother with two jobs, a sold out grail, a confirmation screen printing like a certificate
The bell rang for a decision nobody had announced yet. Morning light on white stone, a cupola, every pigeon in the park up
One gold tooth, zero shame, a full understanding of the camera. A Union Square railing, a tourist outmaneuvered, a bird holding the pose
A wing on a shoulder ends a war nobody remembers starting. A girder above the tracks, the Pigeon Queen, a new rat king
For one night every countdown clock in the system agreed to the second. A platform podium, a tailored MTA coat conducting, each train arriving as a chord

works.t: The Rat King Meets the Machines
works.s: Machines came to the rail asking for terms, and Squab gave them. A cashmere coat, a bent bottle cap crown, a third rail dark and safe
She kneels on Chelsea pavement in her good coat to see properly. Eye flowers pushing up through a subway grate, wool against concrete
The city built a mirror and every eye in it turned at once. A hoisted panel on a Manhattan face, a crowd below meeting its own gaze
Thrifted couture photographs better than the real thing at golden hour. A Chinatown roof, water tower slats, the Manhattan Bridge arch behind everyone
Squab holds his first full court under Delancey, everyone seated as equals. Rats and machines and pigeons on cashmere benches, the crown of light left beside him unworn
Train and operator finished the last run in complete agreement. Terminal lights ahead, a cab lit low, a shift ending on time for once

works.t: The Rat Court Sits in Session
works.s: Machines took seats at the Court as equals and nobody argued. A disused platform, lantern light, enormous shadows on the tile behind everyone
It practised until the nod was exact, then spent it well. A subway platform, train lights coming, a man nodded at for once
Two strangers split a fare and trade entire lives by the bridge. Lower East Side to Queens, a meter running, no names exchanged
At four in the morning the old city handed over the watch. Lamplighters and androids and streetlights passing one small flame down the Williamsburg Bridge until the ferry sounded

works.t: The Old King and the Old Machine
works.s: Two retirements sat down together and neither one filled the silence. A Coney Island yard, rust, Atlantic wind moving the weeds around a dead subway car

works.t: The Drop That Chose Its Owners
works.s: The jacket could not be bought, only found. Folded on stoops and subway seats in all five boroughs at one dawn minute, already fitted to its finder
The season's most celebrated debutante runs a crane by daylight. Hudson Yards, white gloves on the levers, a tiara hanging from the cab mirror

works.t: The Handoff at the Bodega Door
works.s: The sign flips from open to open and the whole city fits in the doorway. A cashmere driver holding it for a kid in box fresh sneakers, the cat on the counter
He came back to buy the block still wearing the store's old apron. Washington Heights, register glow, a cat entirely unimpressed by the transaction

works.t: The Taxi That Came Back Vintage
works.s: It went out for one fare and came back two decades in both directions. Nineteen seventies paint over hover skirts, a diner curb, a driver leaning on the roof
Eleven at night, alone, and the pizza turned to face him. Penn Station heat lamps humming a chord, orange light on the counter tile
Two ranks on the bridge at sunrise, and one small thing crossing between them. Machines on one side, people and rats and pigeons on the other, a child receiving

f5_west.name: The Originals
f5_west.why: Era I. The founding census: legends, neighbours, places, villains. The MoMA keeps Van Gogh here; we keep the first 766.

works.s: The whole city passes through and nobody makes eye contact. The tile, the turnstile, the wait measured in incoming rumble
The line has a god and he glows in the tunnel dark. The psychedelic ghost, the tunnel deity, the spirit the third rail feeds
It moves the whole city and apologizes for none of the delay. The platform, the rumble, the closing doors that wait for no one
The stage moves between stops and the crowd can never leave. The mariachi, the doo-wop, the drum that fills the moving car
How am I doing, he asked the whole city, and meant it. The mayor, the subway platform, the chutzpah that defined a decade
The checkerboard cab hauled the city before the medallion cost a fortune. The Checker, the old yellow, the fare from a slower New York
Raise an arm and a stranger takes you anywhere for the meter. The medallion, the hail, the off-duty light that ruins your night
The city's poor man's paradise still runs on salt and adrenaline. The boardwalk, the wooden Cyclone, the sideshow at the end of the train
He owns the bodega and lets the humans think they run it. The counter perch, the mouser, the boss the health code ignores
A nickel hot dog outlived every empire on the boardwalk. The frank, the crinkle fries, the Coney counter open since 1916
The face you nod to for years and never name. The stoop regular, the night block, the neighbor the eye-flowers watch
She gives directions all day from a booth the city keeps closing. The glass booth, the pointed finger, the last human help on the platform
Something luminous rides the current between the stations. The glow, the tunnel, the ghost the trains carry but never catch
He naps on the chip rack and dares you to move him. The perch, the nap, the mouser who clocks out whenever he wants
He sends the flock up and trusts the whole block to come home. The coop, the flight, the old Brooklyn hobby on the tar roof
He masters the lean that needs no pole and never falls. The middle-distance stare, the ride, the balance every local earns standing
He steers the only free ride with the best view in the harbor. The Staten Island run, the wheel, the skyline twice a shift
Meet me at the corner means everything and no exact spot. The street sign, the lean, the wait that starts every night out
Every local avoids the one place the whole world visits. The billboards, the crush, the lights too bright to ever call night
Another key, another notice, another winter decided upstairs. The papers, the night city, the landlord the block never sees
The biggest marquee in the city still means an event. The neon, the great stage, the art deco palace that swallows a crowd
The 7 train runs past every flag on earth. The neon, the late shift, the borough where the whole planet clocks out
