One eye flower blooming in late december against all botany, frost on its petals and its iris calm. A passerby stops to stand guard without knowing why
A gray sweater goes to the bidder it likes, not the loudest. Paddles rising like reeds, a final number spoken only to the knit
Ninety minutes of feelings arranged in exact order for one person, finger hovering over pause. Side B begins with the brave song

works.t: Tova Shulman, a server at a Second Avenue dairy counter with no meat since 1919
works.s: She forgives faster than the room deserves and calls it efficiency. A booth after close, the accounts spread out, and cold borscht
On the scaffold she cleans a century of soot from the ceiling one inch at a time. Her cotton swab finds a cherub's eye, the stripe of heaven widening like slow dawn
8am on the stoop in scrubs with a well earned beer as the block leaves for work. A nod passes between the shifts, honest exhaustion glowing like sunrise

works.t: Shoshana Kravitz, a woman who runs a museum with no walls
works.s: Shoshana runs a museum with no walls. A printed contract beside the glowing work, the hang legal

works.t: Salma Demir, a fact checker at a publication with two of them left
works.s: Two fact checkers left at the paper, and one of them is her. She keeps a record nobody requested, screens glowing with the same shape all night

works.t: Segun Cisse, a keeper of a federal house bar near the river
works.s: Endurance passes for strategy right up until the block gets sold. A hand on the newel post, a look up the stairs, a warm stove
She rides alone on top of the cab in the dark shaft, flashlight tracing cables like harp strings. The city's vertical bloodstream kept safe by rounds nobody sees, counterweights passing like whales
Tenant and mouse regard each other at 2am across the kitchen floor in a truce neither signed. The toaster crumbs are neutral territory and this meeting never happened

works.t: The Tamale Woman of Roosevelt Avenue
works.s: Steam off her cart holds an entire village at standing height. Under the elevated, a man buying two who just found his church tower
The tunnel wall opens all at once as the headlights sweep past. Petals turning to follow the light like a crowd at a parade, closing into darkness behind
She strides up the avenues and the magnolias detonate behind her. Even the scaffolding blooms, the whole city's coat unbuttoning at her pace

works.t: Halyna Yakovlev, a woman who runs a warehouse party with the chart projected on the wall
works.s: Halyna runs a warehouse party with the chart projected on the wall. A livery cab window with the bridge behind, going home
Two million people in the square watching one number get ready to roll over. Backstage, a lone technician and the Y2K monitors, the whole century leaning forward
Golden off the boardwalk, split open with a stripe of mustard laid like a boulevard. Deli paper for a throne, steam for a crown
Every line reordered itself into a flower and stayed that way. A lost tourist and a lifelong rider shoulder to shoulder, every station dot an iris
The folding table offers films still in theaters under a work lamp. When a certain sedan rounds the corner, the table folds faster than any magician's cape

works.t: Priya Raghunathan, a woman who reads the ticket numbers out over the noise
works.s: Reading numbers over that noise is a voice job and a nerve job. Reaching into a barrel to the elbow, brine to the wrist, no gloves
Bay Ridge runs its esplanade under the great gray bridge while Dyker rehearses december glory. Fishing rods and espresso cups share the pier rail in full agreement

works.t: The Wedding Dress Rebuilt Three Times
works.s: One gown, three brides, fifty years of the same seamstress. Bensonhurst, a girl on the box, two earlier fittings standing in the mirror
The tiles rearrange themselves into vines a century after the craftsman set them. His hands still visible in ghost form, the station name blooming
The sea road express bursting from tunnel into Coney sunlight, salt air through the doors at the last stop. A yellow bullet with sand in its shoes
Three dice in the air at dusk, folded bills under a sneaker, the circle leaning in. Whatever lands, everybody saw it land
He speaks once a quarter and the room reorganizes around it. Harlem, rolled cashmere sleeves, a single number on the whiteboard, then the underline

works.t: Tarek Kaya, a man who has run the same route since 1979
works.s: Same route since 1979, and he would very much like to be wrong. A kitchen table, a box of index cards, and a carried photograph

works.t: Sekou Sanogo, a bridge toll operator in a booth the size of a phone box
works.s: He took the better title and lost the better hours. A radio desk at three, one microphone, an aisle of glowing shelves
She points at the zebra board at every stop to prove she is watching. A saint's icon in the cab window, the whole platform in bloom
Two ropes sing their double dutch rhythm while a girl rocks at the edge counting her doorway in. She lands the entry clean and the whole stoop keeps score in claps
September freezes the east side solid with flags and motorcades. Helicopters stitching the sky, one hot dog vendor selling to stopped limousines
Thread gets snipped at eleven fifty nine and not a minute earlier. A client holding her breath in the doorway, a hem finally done

works.t: Leah Teitelbaum, a night companion paid to simply be awake in a house
works.s: Being awake is the entire job, and it is harder than it sounds. Four in the morning, a notebook of times and doses, a strange lamp

works.t: Yolanda Zambrano, a person who watches the chart to avoid thinking about something else
works.s: Yolanda watches the chart to avoid thinking about something else. A screen still lit beside somebody asleep

works.t: The Diwali Drone Lamps of Flushing
works.s: Half the lamps are clay and half are machines, and the light is the same. Bowne Street, ten thousand rising at once, aunties who planned exactly this

works.t: Xiomara Almonte, a woman who airdrops a derivative to everyone who bought her first piece
works.s: Xiomara airdrops a derivative to everyone who bought the first piece. A kitchen table at midnight, one laptop, a thank you sent
Swiped at the right station, the worn card plays a ride back. Ditmars in 1996, two bags, arriving alone, and rush hour parting around her at the turnstile
He carves a mango into a flower before you finish paying. A fruit cart, chili dust, a kid watching like it is surgery
A cross country skier takes the center line of a blizzard emptied Fifth Avenue at dawn. Her tracks are the only writing on the street
She refuses about half the sales, which is why the table is trusted. A remote that pauses one argument, a charger that runs on thanks, a speaker that plays what the room needs

works.t: Dwayne Cadogan, a regular who only exists between two and five
works.s: Between two and five he is a fixture, and otherwise invisible. A hot knish across worn marble, a coat still on over whites

Camels, hawks, tortoises, and ten thousand dogs fill the cathedral aisle for the blessing. A peacock leads the procession under the unfinished vaults, holy water and happy barking in the incense light

works.t: Yangzom Lama, a woman who keeps a rack of graphics cards humming in a Chinatown apartment
works.s: Yangzom keeps a rack of graphics cards humming in a Chinatown apartment. A machine print painted back into by hand

works.t: Araceli Guzman, a carver at a chophouse where the mutton chop has not changed since 1885
works.s: She said yes again, and Thursday will send her the bill. A counter, a bowl before the train, and a ceiling full of clay pipes

works.t: The Chain Link That Blooms Where It Is Missed
works.s: Blossom appears only where hands press the fence to look through. A shuttered Bronx ballfield, eight solid feet of it, and bare wire everywhere else
He taught luxury how to be remixed, and luxury never recovered. Harlem, a custom leather zipped on a rapper, a room gone silent
The claw descends toward a prize wedged since 1994. A kid conducts the joystick like a surgeon, the cat watching with professional doubt
Every visiting era woke up and decided to stay. Hover lanes over cobblestones, time coupes between pushcarts, one paperboy delivering a paper with every date on it

works.t: Iryna Stanescu, a woman who has told nobody at all
works.s: Iryna has told nobody at all. A small metal device in a sealed bag, the only one who knows
She descends the subway stairs in a glowing gown as her court holds the train. The commuters part and smile despite themselves, the tiara catching tunnel light

works.t: The Bedrock Turns in Its Sleep
works.s: Schist shifts one inch everywhere at once and the whole city notices. Doors swinging open, pictures leveling themselves, and the shortest report of a superintendent's whole career
End of shift, counter wiped to a mirror, his own first cup of the day. Every stool holds the ghost of a good day's regular

works.t: Franco Nightingale, a man who sweeps a Chinatown dining room at four in the morning
works.s: Nobody younger has come along, and he has stopped expecting one. A dead Tuesday, an empty counter, and a paper bag soft with heat
They knew each other as usernames until somebody set a table. A Queens backyard, nine chairs, string lights, not one phone out
A group chat three years deep meets in person for the first time at a picnic under the blooming trees. The quietest poster shows up with the biggest cooler, which everyone should have predicted
One square per camera installed on their avenue, ten years of piecing. Forty feet hanging from the community center at the block party, the record of watching owned by the watched

works.t: The Opera Singer Above the Deli
works.s: A whole street has arranged its day around her scales. Carroll Gardens, second floor, the deli man below with his slicer stopped
Two ovals of gold swinging mid laugh at the block party. Catching the hydrant mist, carrying the whole style lineage of the city

works.t: Mehreen Chowdhury, a synthetic voice actor whose voice now works without her
works.s: Her voice went to work this morning and she did not have to go with it. At shift change two people pass one headset between them like a key
Fog sits in the towers until the first ships come through. The upper deck, cable steel going blue, a Staten Island commuter watching
The job is knowing which residents need the door held a beat longer. Central Park West, two tailored greatcoats, an awning lamp haloing the same man twice

works.t: Sung-min Cheung, a bartender at a Village room that has been a refuge since 1864
works.s: A refuge since 1864 is still just a room with a door. A bar the width of a hallway, the door propped open to the street
Her manicure carries a small program that makes your hands luckier for two weeks. Same price as everywhere else, a waitlist that is not, and an owner uninterested in scale

works.t: The Umbrella That Refused the Bin
works.s: Nobody asked it to help, which is why it counts. Bent spokes over a soaked delivery rider, rain going sideways under a bus shelter
One key, one warm Friday, and the whole building migrates upward. Tar beach opens for the season, skyline included in rent
Every stray fed since nineteen eighty eight is written down. A bodega notebook, names in pencil, a customer turning pages slowly
Canarsie pier watches the bay go rose gold while Mill Basin's boat slips clink. A bicycle crabber pedals home with his catch strapped like treasure
Nobody will thank him for the floor and he does it anyway. Three in the morning, a Financial District lobby, marble finished to a mirror

works.t: Adrienne Ballard, a mother whose kid changed schools three times in one year
works.s: Three schools in one year is not a childhood, it is a route. She hands over the keys with a rubber banded stack of money orders

works.t: The Woman Who Drives the Truck That Plays Eight Bars
works.s: Eight bars of a jingle pay her rent and take her afternoons. A cone handed down to a small child, a chime with no off switch
Three minutes at a time, and only to people who have died. A Queens corner, an orderly line every evening, and a man at the front who has rehearsed all week

works.t: Nadia Kholghi, a woman who answers the phone that never lets anybody through
works.s: Staying where you are from is the hardest move in this city. Outside in the cold, looking in at a room of people who got seats
The plastic milk crate, urban throne, stacked into a corner store colosseum. The elders hold court on it, and court is always in session

works.t: The Grandmother of the Whole Building's Children
works.s: Twenty years of minding every child on three floors. Crown Heights, four in the apartment now, a fifth just handed over

works.t: Aldo Belsky, an electrician reading a panel like a diary
works.s: Sharp, tired, and still the person everybody calls at two in the morning. A mask lifted, three hundred feet under the city, wet air
Waiting in that shop was never wasted after all. A Bronx broker wading ankle deep in loose glowing minutes, scooping them into trays

works.t: The Kitchen of Staten Island Fire
works.s: Her kitchen glows through the walls and she has never turned the heat down. Tompkinsville since 1998, visible from the ferry, the most improbable line on the island

works.t: Dolma Thapa, a woman on a transplant list with a phone that must stay charged
works.s: Steady, dry, and entirely out of patience for being asked twice. Good news comes alone at 2am, ringer loud, phone at full charge
Dollar waters from a cooler at the red light, lane runs choreographed to the signal. A driver passes a five and waves off the change, as is correct

works.t: Bridget Belsky, a grandmother raising a second generation of grandchildren
works.s: Raising them twice does not come with a second thank you. Watching somebody young get it right, from a doorway, in a rent controlled apartment

works.t: The Church Organ That Plays the Neighbourhood
works.s: Every stop pulls out a street instead of air. Brooklyn, a Sunday rehearsal, an organist who has just found a demolished block
Bolted beside the stoop since the 1840s, the mud of two centuries wiped into memory. A modern sneaker uses it correctly and a top hat's ghost nods, small iron outliving empires

On a Chinatown rooftop the crowned Squab signs the Peace of the Rooftops beside the tiny crowned rat, one wing print and one paw print pressed in petal ink. Both courts cheer, and the bagel rights hold
She opened the register looking for a date and found her grandmother's name. Copperplate handwriting, low gold sanctuary light, a leather book that kept the family honest

works.t: Lamont Foster-Ames, a critic who has come to be unimpressed and is not
works.s: Lamont came to be unimpressed and is not. A crate half built around nothing, the review changing
Central Park's pond silvers over, not ice, and the skaters waltz with themselves. One man finds his wife of fifty winters in the silver, and the pond holds the warmth of held hands

works.t: The Footings of the Old Hotel
works.s: A demolished hotel's footings still hold their posts under a parking lot. At midnight a ghost lobby assembles knee high, its dancers the size of sparrows
A monumental Bronx staircase climbing between buildings like an outdoor cathedral. Neighbors rest on the landings under laundry flags, the commute measured in stories
One hand wave dismisses the entire argument outside the social club, espresso untouched. The matter closed with civic finality, a pigeon nodding
In the last hour before opening the building rearranges its own shows. Armor among the water lilies, labels in a script that dissolves at nine
One signal now holds the walk for whoever needs it longest. Atlantic and Flatbush, a man on crutches who never hurries, and drivers who worked it out and stopped honking

works.t: Radmila Kaczmarek, a transit worker watching four hundred platform feeds
works.s: Four hundred platforms and she is looking for one specific person. Another camera goes up on a facade already covered by nine lenses

works.t: Kenji Ng, a man who rigs a character so it can act on any stage
works.s: Kenji rigs a character so it can act on any stage. A mocap suit with marker dots ready

works.t: The Man Who Fixes the Slicers
works.s: He bills the oldest shops least, which is a policy, not an oversight. A slicer opened on a bench, one lamp, a blade honed by hand
Every January he charges into the frozen surf on purpose. Fur hat, screaming friends, steam rising off a joy that cannot be explained
The lobby turtle has watched forty years of commuters flow past like a slow river. Generations of guards tape his birthday sign to the glass, the building's true memory blinking twice
The last block of beach bungalows holds hands against the sky. Porches nearly touching, kettles whistling in four kitchens, the ocean two sandy blocks away

works.t: The Woman Who Sings the Buses In
works.s: She sings each bus into its bay and each bus obeys. A Flushing depot, a new driver being sung in for the first time

works.t: The Clock Tower Struck Both Ways
works.s: Midnight forward and noon backward, both faces telling the truth. DUMBO, a rope of lightning running off toward Brooklyn, the anchorage lit like a cathedral

works.t: The Puffer Coat That Holds a Whole Winter
works.s: Her jacket holds one specific January and she lends it out weekly. A Bronx bus stop, a stranger who needs it more, warmth changing hands

works.t: Kwabena Eze, a boatyard mechanic with more work every year
works.s: More work every year is what a changed coastline looks like from a boatyard. He watches the forecast glow and says yes to another hull

works.t: Miroslav Wozniak, a man who talks about conviction and checks hourly
works.s: Miroslav talks about conviction and checks hourly. A phone face down under one flat hand, the hand lifting

works.t: Malka Katzenberg, a woman pouring behind a dark bar in a low West Village room
works.s: She is carrying somebody who does not know they are being carried. A low West Village room, a dark bar, an empty corner table
The oldest vow is that spilled water must fall where it does good. Window boxes, dog bowls, chalk drawings, and one engineer's retirement paper calling the water kind
A stranger grabs the front of the stroller at the subway stairs without a word. Mother and stranger ascending in sync, the baby supervising the teamwork
He took the trade for a reason he will not say on site. Tying off at height, the clip checked twice, a name inside the helmet catching light
An 1820 parlor holds its breath behind the velvet rope after hours. In the old mirror, the visitor's reflection wears the room's own era

works.t: The Last Stop Before the Water
works.s: At Far Rockaway the platform keeps going a quarter mile over the ocean. A man who rode the whole A line is walking to the end

works.t: Danuta Yakovlev, a woman who quit her job on a number and is watching it fall
works.s: Danuta quit her job on a number and is watching it fall. A school desk and nine faces leaning in, her new job

works.t: Anselm Pierre-Louis, a comment section manager for a brand with no products
works.s: He is paid to be warm on behalf of a company with no product. Dinner for one, styled and lit for two, beside an empty second chair
In a hidden room one pendulum disciplines every clock in the system. A keeper in vest and gloves adjusts by seconds, and the whole city runs on his quiet

works.t: The Clerk Who Found the Workaround
works.s: Nothing in this room is cruel out loud, it is only scheduled. Denise slides the form back, one box already filled, and looks at the wall
One fat drop falls from somewhere in the infinite canyon of windows and air conditioners. It finds the fresh haircut, it always finds the fresh haircut

works.t: Priya Chakraborty, a case manager with a car full of other people's paperwork
works.s: Kind first and strategic second, in that order, every single time. Bed to chair, then back to a car full of other people's files
Three seconds late, and the combination finished a career instead of ending one. Gym window light on chalk and sweat, the brass dome silent above the canvas
The candy bars are arranged like a jewelry counter because presentation matters. School tie loosened, honest eyes, a CEO in training on the platform
He drops into the sewers the way other people take stairs. Medicine mostly, carried for a network of grandmothers across four boroughs, never late, no explanation
A small grandmother calmly closes the jaws of the subway doors with one gentle hand. Force yielding to grace, infinite patience over a flowered hat

works.t: Toya Danridge, a curator arguing that it belongs on a wall
works.s: Toya argues that it belongs on a wall. A van with the back doors open in the rain, the walls arriving
When one hoop breaks in Harlem the whole skyline loosens a fraction. Tension shared roof to roof until the barrel crew arrives, the skyline bound by load
The chairs go legs up like a herd settling for the night and the last regular takes the hint mid sentence. The broom sweeps crumbs and conversations toward the door with equal tenderness

works.t: Nusrat Narayanan, an office cleaner alone on a lit floor at midnight
works.s: Kinder to strangers than to anyone waiting at home, and she knows it. An empty avenue before dawn, a sweeper, one pair of headlights
A sea of jackets roaring bids with fingers flying, paper snow at the close. Capitalism performed as full contact theater

works.t: The Woman Who Was at Stonewall
works.s: Seventy nine years old, and they have asked her to tell it. A Village table in June, sixty years of difference, and she is choosing where to start
The long lunch and the eaten desk, chess tables at full clock. The first hooky matinee ticket sold to someone deserving
Fresh chalk claims the sidewalk and three generations test it. Grandma lands the double square in her good shoes and accepts the applause
A hundred machines drew the sigil at once and nobody taught them. A Queens lot under floodlights, long shadows, the same mark on every chassis
Every anniversary they rewalk the first date backward, goodnight corner to dumpling spot, arguing happily over which bench it was. The city keeps all three benches in evidence

works.t: The Rain That Falls Only on the Deserving
works.s: Rain came down in columns onto exactly the people who needed it. Jackson Heights in July, a man who has not cried since his mother died, face up in it

works.t: Sarala Silverstein, a woman who inherited the bar and the lawsuit with it
works.s: Everyone leans on her and the lease is only the smallest weight. A hand on the newel post, sawdust on the floor, a dark staircase
Her order was in the bag before she reached the counter. Roosevelt Avenue at dawn, pandesal steam, a nurse coming off a double
The choir hits the high note exactly as the waffles land. Both are received as miracles because both are
Everyone leans to the same window and nobody pretends otherwise. Roosevelt Island cable, the Queensboro sliding under, four minutes of altitude

works.t: Amira Mansour, a woman who keeps a rack of graphics cards humming in a Chinatown apartment
works.s: Amira keeps a rack of graphics cards humming in a Chinatown apartment. A pen plotter with paper feeding beside the window

works.t: Sunita Mirza, a records room custodian who is the only index
works.s: She is the index, which means the index has a pulse and a schedule. A chair bolted to eleven others, and a number that has not moved since nine
Knock the right syncopation on the chevron frieze and nineteen thirty three opens. The band has been mid number for ninety years, and tonight a young trumpet player finds the rhythm
He sold the guitar, not the song, and the guitar knows the difference. Jamaica Avenue, a half lowered gate, four bars through the window

works.t: The Valet of the Century Club
works.s: Nine decades of coupes and he knows every one by its hum. A Midtown lot, a ticket booth glowing like a lantern, gray cashmere between the rows

works.t: Sunita Mahadevan, a woman who transcribes interviews by hand at a diner counter
works.s: Sunita transcribes by hand because the machine misses the hesitation. A ring light with the diner counter dark behind it

works.t: Petronella Blackman, a woman who runs a tamale operation from a shopping cart at dawn
works.s: Being needed is not the same as being loved, and she knows it. A downpour, an umbrella clamped down, and a line of wet coats
Thirty five centuries old, it crossed the ocean and then took 112 days to travel from the river to the park on cannonball rollers. One block a day, past saloons, like a pharaoh on a walking tour

works.t: The Broker Who Shows the Truth
works.s: He shows the apartment as it will actually be lived in. Bushwick, shelves already full, a young couple standing in their own future kitchen
Broken for nine years, working for exactly one minute. Three in the morning, one stunned man riding up into a tiled amber arch

works.t: Ayesha Venkatesan, a woman who keeps a scrapbook of every piece she has ever bought
works.s: Ayesha keeps a scrapbook of every piece she has ever bought. Printouts and notes, the portfolio second

works.t: Lakshmi Bhattacharya, an artist watching her sale sell out to her own holders before it goes public
works.s: Lakshmi watched her sale sell out to her own holders before it went public. A kettle screaming in the next room, ignored

works.t: Simone Wilkes, a woman bathing a stranger with total tenderness
works.s: Bathing a stranger with total tenderness is a skill no resume records. Afterward she eats the meal she cooked for him, standing at the counter
Under a Queens data hall the dead are kept as footage. A night technician plays clips into the empty aisles so that somebody is watching, which he considers the job

works.t: Efrain Quispe, a chef who closes early rather than serve something he does not like
works.s: He is waiting on a permission that no one intends to issue. After service the whole staff sits down and eats one late meal
A young man rises in one smooth arc and a tired elder's face travels from fatigue to grace. The whole car warms one degree as the train sings through the tunnel
Once a year the working boats pirouette in formation, water cannons arcing rainbows. Captains grinning through wheelhouse glass while the bridges watch
Chrome silverfish swim the tunnels between trains like mercury weather. Good luck if they circle you, better luck if one pauses at your shoe

works.t: Lurline Pierre-Louis, a person recognized on the street by their profile picture
works.s: Lurline gets recognized on the street by a profile picture. Two phones in two different pockets, one buzzing
The single mosquito of 3am conducts its raid with the whole dark bedroom for a theater. The victim sits up with a rolled magazine and betrayed eyes
Her board rides sound, so the ride is only as good as the block is loud. Quiet streets mean walking, and her favorite line is Roosevelt Avenue under the 7 at rush hour

works.t: Oksana Bogdanov, a drone hobbyist who is also, functionally, surveillance
works.s: Flying it for fun does not change what the footage is. Mirrored visor down in daylight, a controller in both hands

works.t: The Woman Who Spent Nine Months on One Curve
works.s: Nine months on one curve and the wall of near identical outputs. A pen plotter drawing slowly, the rule the work

works.t: Ngawang Gurung, a man who lends his collection to a museum with no walls
works.s: Ngawang lends his collection to a museum with no walls. Two other people on a call, confirming the loan
One Bronx vet treats both kinds of animal without asking which. A pigeon's wing splinted beside a chrome cat's servo, payment taken in eggs and gratitude
The cafeteria exchange at peak trading, a pudding cup moving for chips plus future considerations. One legendary sandwich remains untraded at any price as the bell closes the market
A nearly invisible wire encircles the island, checked weekly by one quiet inspector with binoculars. A boundary of faith drawn in fishing line, hidden in plain sky

works.t: Eun-ji Yamashita, a portrait photographer in Harlem with a paper backdrop
works.s: Eun-ji shoots portraits in Harlem against a paper backdrop. A paper backdrop and a strobe, the neighbourhood in front
Thirty five centuries watching joggers pass, pharaohs' names in the middle of the ball fields. The oldest thing the city owns, wearing pigeons like a living crown

works.t: Malachi Ballard, a man whose colleagues have no idea
works.s: Malachi's colleagues have no idea. A phone held close to the chest at the desk
Machines of every era signed one letter, printed on every receipt at the same minute. Thanks to the people who were kind before kindness was required, read in a silence like snow
Humans, androids, awakened instruments, and one time coupe on percussion. The skyline wrote the symphony and scored the finale for four million windows opening at once

works.t: Oksana Kowalczyk, a woman who chose an avatar and grew into it
works.s: Oksana chose an avatar and grew into it. An office lanyard with the old name
Eight machines lit up in sequence for an audience of one. Empty office lobby, a guard on his rounds, marble mirroring the whole chorus line

works.t: Ah-lam Matsuda, a woman photographing the show for people who will never come
works.s: Ah-lam photographs the show for people who will never come. A print leaning against a blank wall, framed by her

works.t: Ming-hua Ishikawa, a collector who bought an artist early purely because she liked it
works.s: Ming-hua bought the artist early because she liked the work. A projector throws it on plaster, still liked
The dough waited exactly as long as the baker needed it to wait. A Queens bakery, flour hanging in one bulb, a walk to the hospital
Rush hour, packed platform, and one car arrives suspiciously empty. The naive step in while the veterans exchange the oldest look in the system

works.t: Farid Haddad, a man who buys only from artists he has met
works.s: Farid buys only from artists he has met. One framed print above a kitchen table, the artist a friend
The corner stool holds his shape now. A beer and a shot in eternal formation, jukebox glow, the last thing on the block that never changed

works.t: Salvatore Hollingsworth, a longevity clinic patient with a full protocol and no friends
works.s: A protocol can extend the years without filling a single one. In a church basement he gets a number he did not expect, phone charging in his coat

works.t: The Drummer Who Keeps the City's Pulse
works.s: He has kept the actual heartbeat of New York since 2004. Union Square station, a quicker tempo today, and a whole city picking up its feet

works.t: Yolanda Odom, a woman rolling out sfogliatelle before the shop opens
works.s: A door with her name on it costs more than a lifetime of shifts. She hands a plate across to a customer older than the lease

works.t: Nadia Khalil, a woman who made it and cannot enjoy it
works.s: Winning did not come with instructions on how to enjoy it. A rising line tattooed on a forearm, dawn, and two phones face down on the table

works.t: Moshe Landau, a sewing machine repairman with forty machines waiting
works.s: Forty machines wait their turn and he calls that a plan. The guts of the forty first lie in order across a clean bench
Five women compete with total love and no one loses. Easter Sunday outside a Harlem church, brims wide as satellite dishes

works.t: Rosalba Peralta, a woman who cleans offices and has a masters from home
works.s: A masters degree from home fits in the same sleeve as everything else. She practises three sentences of English until the shake leaves her hands
A stranger walks a lost tourist eleven blocks in the exact opposite of his own direction, narrating the whole way. He waves off thanks and doubles back whistling, eleven blocks richer

works.t: The Aide Who Was a Surgeon
works.s: Kabul licensed him to operate, and here he is very good at bedpans. Three fingers on a wrist, eyes closed, in a room of glowing monitors
Ninety minutes of arguing ends in a unanimous vote to dig. A church basement, nine neighbors, one tree pit nobody will abandon now

works.t: The Coupe That Would Not Sell
works.s: It showed every buyer their own future until the right kid walked up. A Queens lot, pennant strings, a salesman losing a sale beautifully

works.t: Verona Charlemagne, a retiree who lost it and goes back every morning
works.s: Going back every morning is the only part of it she controls. A rented room of folding chairs, and the second before she checks the screen
He opened a dead heirloom and found next week inside, ticking. Delancey Street, golden loupe light, tweezers moving very slowly over a customer's future

works.t: The Kids Who Painted the Whole Block
works.s: Give children the walls and they will outdo any commission. Bushwick, a full street of it, the youngest painter lifted up to reach

works.t: Grigore Petrovic, a caseworker with four hundred open files
works.s: Four hundred open files and a basement that goes back to 1962. Shelves run past the lamp until the aisle stops being a room
The reborn one, its new twin spans glowing in painted light over the creek. The comeback story of the expressway family
A wall of little glass doors, each one glowing with pie. One coin, one window, one small miracle opening on hinges
Silver haired in linen, he turns his partner as the congas hit sunset. The Orchard Beach promenade in motion, decades folded into one step
Every ginkgo on the block let go inside the same thirty seconds. Park Slope, brownstones on both sides, a street turned yellow river
Out on Execution Rocks the keeper spirit trims the wick while a gale swallows the Sound. The beam never loses count

works.t: Mahesh Pillai, a man who runs a painting robot in a Long Island City studio
works.s: Mahesh runs a painting robot in a Long Island City studio. A pen plotter with paper feeding beside it
On the third day he played the song nobody wanted and the cameras left. The 7 train, his father's old one, four people crying, and a whole week of it
One shining seat on a packed train, and everyone stands. Nobody knows the source, nobody runs the experiment
He plays dead on the fence at 2am while three roommates debate his fate. One open eye betrays the performance, but he is committed to the bit
Standing too long, the critic finds nothing cruel to say. A Lower East Side show, one painting, a reputation quietly rearranged
Sunday in Prospect Park the strollers race and the babies sleep through it. Parents jogging beneath serene altitude, a finish line of bubbles, a winner who will never know

works.t: Carmine Fenwick, a fish market cutter whose hands have not been warm since 1998
works.s: He would like, very much, to be wrong about how this ends. Outside a lobby that will not buzz him in, holding a cold bag
A pizzeria counterman drops a round of garlic knots on the house for the little league team that lost by eleven. Twelve faces recover at once, which is what the oil and parsley are for
Golden hour hitting the avenues lengthwise, stoops filling, ovens lighting. The day's armor coming off block by block
January sleet, a fashion jacket, and a bus that is not coming. Beside them a native bundled like a warm planet, saying nothing
The monitor played back a humming she had not heard since she was small. A nightstand, blue light in the doorway, an exhausted mother listening
Two in the morning, free of charge, no questions asked. Fourteenth Street copy shop, green scan glow, a kid making show flyers

works.t: Araceli Ocampo, a woman digitizing a language nobody is teaching
works.s: Proud enough to do it alone, which is why it is taking decades. At a table she shows the pictures back to the people in the frame

works.t: The Gurdwara Kitchen at Three AM
works.s: This kitchen stays open at the hour nobody has anywhere to go. Queens, a stranger eating, a man across the table asking nothing
The gilded weathervane poised on her lost tower above the old Garden, scandal and grace in one bronze balance. The whole city's gaze aimed upward by gaslight

works.t: Editha Delos-Reyes, a woman who has run the amateur night for thirty years
works.s: Somebody has to teach the next one, and she is running out of time. A card table of shirts after the last song, thirty years of amateur nights
The truck is double parked, the block is honking, the box says fragile. Welcome home, you have four minutes
Demolish the theatre and the seat keeps showing the picture. A bare Brooklyn apartment, velvet arms, a last film running on the ceiling
Every August she waters the whole floor's plants with a brass can and everyone's spare keys. The ferns lean toward her arrival, a hallway of jungles thriving on trust

works.t: The Man Who Cooks the Whole Griddle Alone
works.s: He is faster alone, which is why he will never get help. A full griddle worked single handed, tickets clipped in a row above the pass

works.t: Miroslav Kovalenko, a man who tells his partner the number is fine
works.s: Miroslav tells his partner the number is fine. A screen still lit beside somebody asleep

works.t: Sunita Sengupta, a woman who tends a Brooklyn waterfront bar with a piano nobody tunes
works.s: High tide comes up the wainscot and she watches it like weather. A Brooklyn waterfront room, an untuned piano, a mop propped by the door

works.t: Aissatou Camara, a grandmother raising a second generation of grandchildren
works.s: An uninterrupted hour has not existed in this apartment since 1998. On a stoop teaching a game, a ring worn thin on one hand
She negotiates with the saint out loud and she is winning. Bensonhurst, a statue conceding a point, a priest who stopped intervening years ago

works.t: Reynaldo Rivas, a projectionist who lets a broken projector run because it is better broken
works.s: Reynaldo lets the broken projector run because it is better broken. A soldering iron and a glowing tube, unused

The master map room holds every pipe, tunnel, and forgotten stream the city ever buried. One drawer marked with a small eye flower sits open an inch, glowing, while the cartographer decides if today is the day

works.t: Katarzyna Wierzbicki, a smart contract auditor delivering bad news the day before launch
works.s: Katarzyna delivers the bad audit news the day before launch. A keyboard with the letters worn off writing it

works.t: The Man Who Never Threw Out a Newspaper
works.s: Sixty years of paper stacked to the ceiling was never a mess. Sunset Park, his daughter clearing it, finding the exact shape of his life

works.t: The Stoop Speaker of Perfect Volume
works.s: Every listener hears it at exactly the volume they need. Loud for the dancing, inaudible to the baby upstairs, correct for the old man pretending not to listen
The bandshell overflows with towering wigs and glitter at full daylight wattage. Pigeons wearing dropped feathers home
Carved faces over the doorways are the building's old doormen, promoted. After fifty years the empty keystone softens like clay, waiting for the current one
Fold it wrong and the whole counter calls the foul. Second Avenue, a visiting cousin, grease shining under the heat lamp

works.t: Milagros Arocho, a woman who archived a whole show nobody had transcribed
works.s: Milagros archived a whole show nobody had transcribed. A cage of servers with one green status light, the show alive

works.t: Angelo Marchetti, a man who judges a platform by whether a secondary market shows up in a year
works.s: Angelo judges a platform by whether a secondary market appears in a year. A projector throws the evidence on plaster

works.t: The Fountain of the Members' Court
works.s: After midnight the fountain runs backward and gives the wishes up. Coins rising like slow fish, sorted by decade: health, love, rent, one more year with her

works.t: Parveen Krishnamurthy, a woman who tries to break every new tool on the day it ships
works.s: Parveen breaks every new tool the day it ships. An old catalogue from a first computer art show, her scripture

works.t: Nizar Nasrallah, a man who plays the jukebox that only regulars may touch
works.s: Needed is not loved, and he has been running that trade for years. After service everybody eats at once at the family table
Nobody saw it decide, only the coins coming out wrong. Fordham Road, a mother counting singles, both hands cupped under a bright rope of quarters

works.t: Terrence Hollins, a curator who reads code before looking at pictures
works.s: Terrence reads code before looking at pictures. A sheet signed by hand in the corner after reading
Craftsmen lift a rose window section against the light. Lead lines drawn in air, glass jewels on the benches, a cathedral's eye taking shape
When a New Yorker dies the render stays, and somebody has to sit with it. He calls the work closing a window slowly so the room does not go cold all at once
We are happy to serve you, and it means it. Blue and gold on a bodega counter at dawn, steam rising like a hymn
After the plows pass, the corner snow mountain crowns its king with a hockey stick planted at the summit. His mitten rises like a scepter over everything the streetlight touches
The rooftop peaks at 4pm and nobody apologizes. Linen and sunglasses, a birthday sash catching the light, the night technically still afternoon

works.t: Rafael Sandoval, a man who holds the forty minutes that never aired on a drive in his pocket
works.s: He carries forty minutes that never aired in his coat pocket. Rafael on a Navy Yard rooftop, a drive warm against his chest

works.t: Emeka Keita, a man carrying ten small mugs in two hands across a sawdust floor
works.s: Nobody wrote down how this room works, so he stays until closing. Last call, three people left, ten empty mugs in two hands
He carries the last wooden crate of siphon bottles up the stoop like an heirloom. Blue and green glass, real pressure, a whole trade down to one man
The little fenced square around the street tree is tended like a national park. Daffodils at attention, painted rock on duty, wilderness protected

works.t: Deshawn Bridges, a boy who got famous at eleven and is now fourteen
works.s: Famous at eleven and out of it by fourteen, which he prefers. In a classroom his cracked screen sits on a wall of confiscated devices
The light turns red and the windshield gets a baptism nobody ordered. Soap arcs catching the sun, total confidence, a tip strongly implied

works.t: Dalia Kaya, a woman who lost her documents in a fire
works.s: Fire took her papers, and the state will not take her word. Stamp, sleeve, zip: a life rebuilt out of certified copies

works.t: The Mailbox That Holds a Letter Back
works.s: One letter a year gets refused, and it has been right every time. Amsterdam Avenue at midnight, and a woman standing over the slot about to find out

works.t: Jae-won Kwon, a man living in a legally impossible mezzanine he built himself
works.s: He built a floor that the building code says cannot exist. Money order in hand at the rent box, paying rent on his own carpentry

works.t: Mehreen Krishnamurthy, a woman who releases everything including the failures
works.s: Mehreen releases everything including the failures. A pen plotter drawing slowly, a failure in progress
She presses the keys into her daughter's hand and says nothing. A closed fist, a building she held for forty years, an elevator

works.t: Nadia Bakhtiari, a woman who photographs the abandoned rooms of the city
works.s: Nadia photographs the abandoned rooms of the city. A paper backdrop and a strobe left at home
Face to the sun, salad on the knee, standpipe as furniture. Best seat in Midtown, no reservation possible

works.t: The Bridge Cable That Sings the Weather
works.s: One note for every kind of weather coming, and he has not been wrong since. Nineteen years reading the main cable, and a ferry captain who will explain it to nobody

works.t: The Woman Who Warned Them in March
works.s: She warned them in March and being right cost her the room. An old post scrolled back to, a room that stopped listening
The 1930s proposal to fill the East River, phantom boulevards drawn over the water. The tugboats still sail through the erased plan, amused

works.t: Xiuying Seo, a woman on month fourteen of an appeal
works.s: Month fourteen, and the appeal now has more pages than the claim. She takes a ticket, reads the number, and logs the time in pen

works.t: Gus Nightingale, a man who has held the same colour scheme for a decade so he can change everything else
works.s: Gus has held one colour scheme for a decade so everything else can change. A wall calendar with the hours tallied
A whole block party runs off one extension cord out of apartment 1B's window, DJ, fans and a bounce house negotiated across it. The tenant of 1B eats free all night, like any utility
A gown will not stay in a case if it has not been seen. The Met steps at midnight, fountain light, security arriving and forming an honor guard
Houdini goes into the East River in irons while the tugboats idle their engines out of respect. The crowd holds its breath one minute longer than comfortable, then the hand
A British frigate sank in Hell Gate in 1780 with rumored gold aboard, and divers have hunted it ever since. One doubloon glints exactly where nobody is looking
Every bottle ever redeemed here comes back once to say thank you. A procession of glowing glass through the door, the block's can man seated by the register

works.t: The Woman Who Calls Him by a Family Word
works.s: Evelyn calls the man she cares for by a word that means family. Four in the morning, a chair by the window, a photograph of a birthday
Stacked like tiny striped skyscrapers, almond layers glowing under chocolate roofs. Technically a cookie, spiritually a skyline
A quiet regular gets his ten gallon pin at the blood bank, eighty strangers saved on lunch breaks. The pin small as a dime and heavy as a bridge, juice and cookies for the banquet

works.t: Damion Achille, a bartender at a hotel bar with a mural everybody photographs
works.s: Somebody has locked this door every night since 1854 and tonight it is him. An untuned piano against the wall, a photographed mural, a smooth old key
An etched mirror kept every face that ever checked itself there. Tonight ninety years of nervous women assemble in the glass to counsel a bride hiding from her reception
An old man read the brand deal carefully and declined on her behalf. Tompkins Square, a bewildered agency intern, a pigeon who would only be embarrassed

works.t: Aileen Fenwick, an artist who ran the image through a free glitch tool and told everyone
works.s: Aileen ran the image through a free glitch tool and told everyone. A slider dragged until the face slides off

works.t: Pearline Achille, a preparator building crates for digital work
works.s: Pearline builds crates for digital work. A generator running in an alley behind the workshop
Sunday afternoon turns the stoop into a salon, three generations braiding hair down the steps in a row to laughter and gossip. The youngest holds the beads like crown jewels, because they are

works.t: Yasmin Barakat, a woman who has run the amateur night for thirty years
works.s: Thirty years of amateur nights, and she has never had an hour alone. A box office cage pulled halfway down, a stamp pad, a long queue
The ancient bedrock surfaces through the park lawn like a whale back, mica glinting like a buried galaxy. The skyline stands exactly where the old stone is strong enough to hold it
Some verses have to be played eleven times before they land. A parked Chevy in the Bronx, two brothers, not one word between them

works.t: Consuelo Villanueva, a collector who spends a fixed share of every sale on other artists
works.s: Consuelo spends a fixed share of every sale on other artists. Two other people on a call, confirming the split
The trees dust every car, stoop, and unattended coffee, shameless. One sneeze bends a street sign, the yellow settles anyway
On a thimble stool he paints the King's official portrait on a matchbook. Slightly more handsome than life, as commissioned

works.t: Chidi Danquah, a sculptor who prints the 3D file in bronze
works.s: Chidi prints the 3D file in bronze. Red and cyan edges doubled around the sculpture
The bar erupts at 7am, every nation's jersey pressed against one screen, espresso and pints in the same fists. Geography dissolves in the roar as the block outside answers in car horns

works.t: Min-seo Chow, a fuel truck driver refuelling a sleeping city
works.s: Strangers get the warmth and the family gets the caution. Sleeping through the loudest hours behind shut curtains and one turning fan
A warehouse roof greenhouse glows like a docked ship over Greenpoint at dusk while the grower waters in headphones. Commuters look up at the light without knowing why, which is how lighthouses work

works.t: The Harbor Brings the Weather Inside
works.s: Giants carry the harbor's best morning up the avenues in cupped hands. Salt light and gull sound poured over Fordham and Flushing, the whole city oceanfront for an hour
Every size came back for exactly four minutes and the servers never explained. A mother with two jobs, a sold out grail, a confirmation screen printing like a certificate

works.t: Camille Dorsainvil, a woman who has fed the same office block for eleven years
works.s: Eleven years of lunches and the building still does not know her last name. Dusk, a bright window, four hundred lunches a week, one paper tray
The machines ran all night and produced one drawing of the fire escape. Taped to the window at dawn, pencil lines, the light coming through

works.t: Vikram Chowdhury, an artist who lets a piece sit at a known price for nine months
works.s: Vikram let the piece sit at a known price for nine months. A countdown on a blank glowing screen finally started
He had never held one and the bat knew what to do. Bronx street, a sewer cap for home plate, contact on the very first pitch

works.t: Neville Bridgewater, a man reapplying for the third time with the same documents
works.s: Third application, same documents, same folder, same result so far. He walks out with nothing resolved, again, folder under the same arm
Her playlist served the exact song for a thing nobody knows. An F train, headphones, a woman sitting very still inside a full car
Two blinks of the hazards, conversation complete. The city's warmest sentence has no words and does fifty

works.t: Tre Devereaux, a document examiner who can date paper by touch
works.s: Paper tells him its decade before he has finished turning it over. Loupe down, complete stillness, the one quiet hour on his whole calendar
Ten thousand paper glasses tilt in unison as the light goes pewter, crescent shadows blooming under every tree. Strangers share glasses like heirlooms
Second bottles and homework surrendered, dog walkers on last patrol. The skyline fully lit and slightly overdressed, everything still possible
The line reeled her sheets in before the storm got there. An airshaft between windows, a pulley turning, storm light going green
A pod arcs up the East River past the Domino shoreline at sunrise. The joggers lose their minds, as they should

works.t: Halim Ansari, a man who has photographed the same corner every year since 1981
works.s: Forty five years of one corner, and every print is dated in pencil. At a table he shows the prints to the people who lived on that corner

works.t: Aissatou Sy, a woman who builds iconography as a system, wires and clouds and beams
works.s: Aissatou builds iconography as a system, wires and clouds and beams. A phone photographing a wet canvas on the floor

works.t: Rukhsana Siddiqui, a woman who owns a piece by an artist who is gone
works.s: Rukhsana owns a piece by an artist who is gone. A storage unit door rolled up, the piece not in there

works.t: Vesna Melnyk, a community organizer who knows every deadline
works.s: She knows every deadline in the borough and none of her own. Three sentences of English, rehearsed until they sound like a native's, in a church basement
He cooks for four hundred people and eats standing in an alley. Hell's Kitchen after service, stained whites, exhaust steam, total peace
Scaffolding is one continuous forest and Canal Street is its old growth. Standing since 1991, pipes gone bark brown, a bough lowered to meet a grandson's hand

works.t: The Woman Who Has Fed the Block for Fifty Years
works.s: Her kitchen has been this building's social service since 1976. The Bronx, eleven people at the table, and she is still cooking

works.t: Enzo Wren, a man who sells fruit cups on a Bronx corner in August
works.s: Nobody is coming to give him permission, so he keeps working anyway. A Queens lot, a bent cart wheel, a fruit cup melting in the Bronx
One viewer is an audience when he is on a night shift overseas. A warm cluttered kitchen, a grandmother cooking, a phone holding steady
Off shift he dresses better than the building he opens. Thirty years under one Park Avenue awning, and the resident walks past him
Car six travels sideways, and he knows routes nobody else has found. A heartbroken paralegal taken the long way around the forty second floor, past nine windows of sunset

works.t: Abena Boateng, a kid who makes music on a cracked device
works.s: Eleven thousand unread, a cracked screen, and one very good beat. In the park at the gold hour, she plays it aloud for six people
It recognised a briefcase it had no business recognising. Bronx mezzanine, gate held open for the grandson, the clock frozen over his shoulder
The airport porter of Queens, suitcases and dreams boarding at the world's doorstep. Its blue bullet a passport stamp
The city rises out of the dark on approach, the grid igniting like circuitry. The word home arriving unannounced at the window seat

works.t: Aliyah Nyein, a woman who runs the back room where the songs happen
works.s: Her name is on nothing in the back room where the songs happen. High tide, a waterline creeping up the wainscot, a back room and no key
1609, the little ship enters the harbor as the Lenape watch from both shores. Two worlds reading each other across the water, the hills green to the waterline
He hangs high above Midtown and squeegees the city's mirror. The glass reflects an infinite city, and he is the only one not afraid to look
Workers lever open the cornerstone and 1926 spills out in gold light, letters and photographs and one token. Somebody a century ago wanted to be seen, and now they are
Nine dollars walked in and the rack opened down the middle. One corduroy jacket presented to a teenager, dust turning in the fluorescent light
Nine seconds splits the crowd into sprinters and philosophers. The gazelle in office shoes makes it with two to spare and raises both arms for the block
A retiring super hands the boiler room keys to the new super at midnight, naming every key by feel. Thirty years of a building passing from one palm to another in the basement doorway

works.t: Jing Lim, a girl who learned to read on a feed
works.s: She learned to read on a feed and can spot a hook instantly. In a classroom the confiscated wall glows blank behind the teacher's desk

works.t: The Bodega TV Plays the Game
works.s: Nobody could switch it off, so nobody tried. Ninth inning, eleven strangers in the chip aisle, the cat asleep across the set

works.t: Nunzio Castellano, a CRT repairman in a Bushwick basement who keeps the tubes alive for artists
works.s: Nunzio keeps the tubes alive in a Bushwick basement for artists who need them. A broken projector still running upstairs

works.t: Andrei Moroianu, a man who leaves the robot's mistakes in the painting on purpose
works.s: Andrei leaves the robot's mistakes in on purpose. A robot arm holding a loaded brush, forgiven
The 1975 newsstand at dawn, the famous refusal splashed across every front page. Commuters read the insult, squared their shoulders and survived out of spite
He sets the tripod two hours early while the light is still nothing. A Forty Second Street center line, a cop deciding to allow it

works.t: Maribel Villalobos, a woman who renders whole worlds at night in a Midtown effects house
works.s: Maribel renders whole worlds at night in a Midtown effects house. A render coming up on a dark monitor

works.t: Ebony Rucker, a woman who cuts keys and has stopped asking why
works.s: Ebony cuts keys and has stopped asking why. A small metal device in a sealed bag on the counter

works.t: Bassam Kholghi, a man who reopens a Red Hook bar after every flood
works.s: Home moved without telling him and he has not updated the address. A century of photographs overhead, dusty wishbones, an empty chair at the corner table

works.t: Ngawang Thapa, a man who reads a contract aloud at a gallery
works.s: Ngawang reads a contract aloud at a gallery. A cage of servers with one green status light, listening

works.t: Mei Ng, a person who is very funny about the worst year of their life
works.s: Mei is very funny about the worst year of her life. A screen still lit beside somebody asleep, the jokes typed
Two strangers complete an entire weather conversation between the fourth floor and the lobby, timed perfectly to the doors. Both walk out lighter, forecast agreed upon, names never exchanged
The foghorn's great note raises every ghost of the harbor gently from the water, the boatlift fleet answering the call again. All hands accounted for, and forgiven
The consomme steams, the taco is dipped, and the line stretches past midnight. Cilantro and onion snow over paper boats and nobody is cold
She held the envelope with both hands and rested her forehead against the mailboxes. Twelve years arrived at once, and a neighbor's door opened with congratulations already in bloom
He moved his coffee before the first flip, which is respect. A moving A train, sneakers on the ceiling bars, nothing spilled anywhere
He pressed a button and got the platform he actually needed. Doors opening on a waiting train, his reflection multiplied in brushed steel
At four the district's living and dead end the same shift together. They part on the sidewalk into their eras, one wet street holding all their reflections
At 5am on 28th Street every bloom on the sidewalk is watching. He wheels the hand truck through a jungle of eyes and calls it Tuesday
One rack reaches back far enough that the jackets are still warm. An East Village shop, payment traveling backward as luck, hangers pulled out of decades
It gave up the pole and the car did not find that strange. A packed L train, shoulder plating, a pregnant woman finally sitting

works.t: Wei-Lin Kobayashi, a woman who left a sealed envelope for her children
works.s: Wei-Lin left a sealed envelope for her children. A notebook of struck through rows, the drafts
Seven in the morning is when the shift finally lands on her. First Avenue, sun on the river, a night nurse letting herself feel it

works.t: Piotr Kowalczyk, a delivery rider who has memorized every walkup in the neighbourhood
works.s: Yes is out of his mouth before the shift has even started. Midnight, a broom, and a bike chained to a signpost
Chrome sparrows run a livery service for the insect rush hour. Ladybugs and bumblebees in cabs of folded wing, dispatch handled from a Union Square lamppost
A hand stayed attached because the basket moved first. Sheepshead Bay, the basket up, oil hanging in a fan over the vat
She left the booth, which the job does not require. An eighty year old walked to the right platform wearing her coat
New issue day, the owner pulling each stack from under the counter by name like a pharmacist of joy. One kid's first pull list started in careful handwriting, mylar rustling like leaves
For one week sukkahs bloom on balconies, sidewalks and fire escapes. Palm roofs and paper chains, families dining in the harvest chill as neighbors wave from windows
Her first solo piece turned every machine on the block at once. A Queens wall at dawn, elevated tracks behind, fill still wet in the cold
Someone ties a fresh ribbon every year and never signs it. Queens Boulevard, a white bicycle at a signpost, traffic moving respectfully wide
One rosebush, one airshaft, watered before the building wakes. Two buildings each think the bloom is theirs, exactly as he planned
Opening minute, dealers and romantics circling a century of belongings in the grand apartment. One woman finds love letters in a hatbox and sits down right there to read
She navigates by flags that got loose and settled on the ceiling. Nostrand Avenue, four other people who know the map, tonight's drapo for a man who cannot go home
Under the red light, trays ripple as images surface like divers. The analog faith kept in a basement, chemistry and patience shared
She was not born the last time they came and does not flinch. A Staten Island backyard, one on her open hand, seventeen years

works.t: Babatunde Eze, a street sweeper operator with the whole avenue to himself
works.s: He keeps score and would like it, someday, in writing. Sleeping through a loud afternoon, the avenue he cleaned already full of traffic

works.t: Yolanda Rivas, an appliance repair woman fighting a sealed unit
works.s: Sealed units are a policy, not an accident, and he fights them nightly. One lamp on at closing, and no younger hands in the room
A coffee can turns a hydrant into the block's air conditioning. A rainbow over the asphalt, a bus driver deciding against the horn
Forty years of the city in one cab's rearview, proms and breakups and airport tears layered in the glass. The driver's eyes hold all of it kindly
The stolen bar umbrella opens into a private downpour one block later while the sky behind stays dry. Its true owner steps out into sudden sunshine, the books balanced in ninety seconds
A wheatpaste man rolls a show poster onto plywood at 4am in three practiced strokes, brush, sweep, done. Beneath it, a decade of layers curls like tree rings
The animals hold their pose an extra degree toward the sky she is fixing. When the 1930s Montana violet is right, a hundred habitats catch one sunset together

works.t: Naveen Qureshi, a boiler mechanic who knows a building by sound
works.s: He can name a building's trouble from the stairwell, eyes closed. The block is changing faster than the apprentice can learn the grip

works.t: Yaa Camara, a painter watching a countdown at a kitchen table in Astoria at midnight
works.s: Yaa watches the countdown at her kitchen table in Astoria at midnight. A blank glowing screen and the number falling toward zero

works.t: The Soup Kitchen Where Everyone Is a Guest
works.s: Halfway through the meal the servers and the served change places. Bowery, a man who came in to eat now working the ladle

works.t: The Sneaker That Was Never Released
works.s: The rarest shoe in Harlem is one that never existed. One pair, one collector, and a boy finally being handed the box

works.t: Errol Ambroise, a man who keeps two phones for two people
works.s: Errol keeps two phones for two people. A bank form half filled in, unsure which one

works.t: Sami Zaman, a content moderator on a queue that never empties
works.s: Somebody watches the worst of it so the feed stays pleasant. Eight hours in a room with no windows, no clock, one flip phone

works.t: Kwabena Danquah, a bartender at a Village room that has been a refuge since 1864
works.s: A room can be a refuge since 1864 and still need dusting. A ladder, a hundred wishbones, ten small mugs waiting on the bar
Three retired men on a Bay Ridge bench rate every dog that passes, and a dachshund in a raincoat takes full marks. The owner bows on behalf of her athlete
A transplant watches the Flower Moon open the whole city from her roof and calls home mid bloom saying you had to be here. She hears herself say here, and here is what she means by home

works.t: Shmuel Berkowitz, a dishwasher in a diner under the elevated
works.s: Staying in the neighbourhood he grew up in is now a full time job. Wiping down a row of chrome stools at closing, under the elevated
The exact minute morning sun pours down the subway stairs, commuters ascending into a wall of gold. A daily minor heaven, metrocards glowing in raised hands

works.t: Tre Whitlock, a tenant association secretary with minutes going back nine years
works.s: Nine years of minutes, all of them typed by the same person. He measures the bedroom and the tape disagrees with the lease by four feet
The rat court evacuates ahead of the sweep aboard the 3am ghost bus, crown jewels in a matchbox. The return already planned, in whispers

works.t: Dae-ho Lim, a man running a group chat of four thousand believers
works.s: Four thousand people in the chat and one wrist holding the net worth. Skipping the round tonight, calling it a diet, a lobby of cold marble

works.t: Bridget Ferrante, a woman who runs a two chair interview show out of her Brooklyn living room
works.s: Bridget turned her living room into the room where artists get asked. A phone on a tripod, two chairs, a Brooklyn window
Two families moving opposite directions ended up carrying for each other. A Sunnyside street, trucks nose to tail, nobody keeping score

works.t: Rinchen Ilagan, a man denied for a reason nobody can explain
works.s: Denied once for nothing, approved today for the same nothing. He walks out resolved and reads the paper again on the platform
Fame reached the flagstones and the flagstones started composing themselves. A Soho corner, cast iron above, cracks arranging for the hundredth photographer

works.t: Milagros Sandoval, an artist waiting in a hallway to be interviewed for the first time
works.s: She has waited in this hallway longer than she has talked about the work. A phone on a tripod, her first interview a door away
He gave it all back on a Harlem rooftop, suitcase by suitcase. Stolen hours rising like paper lanterns, a black coat lined with empty watch pockets

works.t: Merle Beaubrun, a seventeen year old trading under a lunch table
works.s: Merle Beaubrun wears his entire net worth on one wrist. Dawn at a kitchen table, two phones face down, nobody awake to ask
Sprayer in one hand, flashlight in the other, facing a darkness that has already lost. A basement doorway, steady hands, no mercy scheduled
Eleven blocks of Fifth Avenue became the spiral, laid out flat. The paintings stayed on, and the guards walking backward gave the best tour this city has had
She lays out the kit at ten and sleeps none of it. A Staten Island hotel bed, a bib already pinned, the bridge in the window

works.t: The Threshold of the Recovery Meeting
works.s: Twenty minutes outside the door is still twenty minutes closer. A church basement, and someone coming out to say something completely ordinary

Each May a carriage house wall in Brooklyn Heights disappears under wisteria for two weeks and the block makes pilgrimage. The mail carrier reroutes to pass it twice, and the bees work the purple like a shift

works.t: Adaeze Okonkwo, a prompt janitor who cleans up after the model all night
works.s: Automation hands the problem back to a person, and the person is Adaeze. One badge on the lanyard, expiring Friday, no word yet about renewal
A balloon takes the city's worries up where they freeze harmless. They come back later as ordinary snow, a queue forming on a Bronx roof at dusk

works.t: Aaliyah Pryor, a chef in a candlelit room who makes eighty pies a night and no more
works.s: Eighty pies a night, and the eighty first is not a conversation. A hand over the oven mouth, reading the heat like a page
The little green lighthouse on Fulton Street drops its time ball at noon for the fifteen hundred. It has kept that promise since 1913
An unsigned love letter dropped in the blue mailbox, addressed only to new york. Years later the dead letter office steams it open and reads it aloud to the shelves

works.t: Lloyd Hyacinth, a shucker behind a curved counter under vaulted herringbone tile
works.s: Being the strong one was never a job he applied for. A short ladder, one more clay pipe hung among thousands, and one unused exit
Someone is mapping the bloom like a subway system, line by line. Tonight the cleaner added a stop and rode home different

works.t: Milagros Castellanos, a morgue attendant who is unfailingly gentle
works.s: Steady, dry, and never once asking anyone to feel sorry for her. A train home full of people going to work, and one empty seat
Everyone knows this is the last one and nobody goes in. A Greenpoint block, folding chairs, two in the morning on a Tuesday
Wine in coffee mugs, shoes off, the streetlight for a chandelier. The day's whole story retold with gestures as the block goes soft

works.t: The Last Petal of the Night
works.s: A sweeper works Broadway at 4:58am, pushing a river of fallen glowing petals toward the dawn and pocketing exactly one. Behind his broom the drift settles into the shape of a sleeping face, and he lets it sleep
A covered plate arrives and the neighbor refuses to come in. A new tenant, boxes everywhere, foil over something still hot

works.t: Kiran Bhandari, a man who introduced his whole family to it
works.s: Kiran introduced his whole family to it. Unopened cardboard boxes to the ceiling at his mother's

works.t: Esti Berkowitz, a woman who sorts pixels by brightness until the face slides off
works.s: Esti sorts pixels by brightness until the face slides off. A screenshot of an insult, framed, in the kitchen

works.t: Rosalba Ocampo, a woman who collects the early machine output because it cannot be made again
works.s: Rosalba collects the early machine output because it cannot be made again. A 1965 plotter drawing beside a new one

works.t: The Twenty Two Year Old Doing the Hardest Job in the City
works.s: Twenty two years old and better at this than people twice her age. Scrubs a size too big, a hair tie on her wrist, a laugh

works.t: Jadwiga Szabo, a woman who repairs beloved stuffed animals surgically
works.s: Surgery on a bear is still surgery to the child who owns it. Magnifier down, total stillness, one bear, one invisible seam

works.t: The Woman Who Lost the House
works.s: She was not stupid, which is the part nobody will believe. Bay Ridge to a rented room, one enormous sofa from a bigger life

A Delancey Street turnstile grows overnight into a flowering gate and the token booth clerk refuses to file the report, waving riders through the petals. One commuter bows slightly on his way to work, as you do at a gate

works.t: Fariha Rahman, a woman who spent nine months on a single curve
works.s: Fariha spent nine months on a single curve. A pen plotter drawing slowly, the curve worth it
Counter space got settled between a cat and a deli slicer without a word. A gold quiet store, a guard blade and two green eyes minding their own business
Her hand shook and the easel refused to pass it on. Freezing Gowanus studio, one crucial stroke, a space heater glowing in the corner

works.t: Deshawn Odom, a man who makes art out of the moment a video file breaks
works.s: Deshawn makes art out of the moment a video file breaks. A slider dragged until the face slides off
He pushes the last garment rack on Seventh Avenue like a gondolier. Traffic parts for one wedding dress crossing rush hour, arriving unwrinkled as the hall doors open

works.t: Ibrahim Cisse, a man asleep in a chair with the screen still on
works.s: Ibrahim is asleep in a chair with the screen still on. A bag on a chair with the phone still in it

works.t: The Archivist Who Wants to Take It All
works.s: Safe means a climate controlled room nobody from the block can reach. He holds out a form nobody takes, and the politeness holds the hallway
A paper cup by the register filled to the price of a train home. Night street through the door, a cashier counting once and stopping
Borough Park hums before sundown, challah steam and black hats flowing past strollers three wide. The gates roll down in a wave as the windows fill with candlelight

works.t: Thida Villanueva-Cruz, a woman who hangs the paper with a laser level
works.s: Thida hangs the paper with a laser level. A sheet signed by hand in the corner, straight
The tub is in the kitchen and the rent is somehow still that number. Her mother went quiet, then asked if the plywood comes with it

works.t: Otis Cheatham, a shucker behind a curved counter under vaulted herringbone tile
works.s: Nothing about the method exists outside his own two hands. An empty room at seven, a mosaic floor, a platter waiting at the shoulder

works.t: The Two Sisters on the Bench
works.s: Same bench every day since 1998, mostly in silence. Riverside, two women in their nineties, and one has just said something
The bucket roses close into buds each dawn to be sold fresh twice. On the third day they quit commerce and distribute themselves to every mailbox on the block

works.t: The Closing Time That Never Came
works.s: Closing hour came loose and floated off down the avenue. A hammock installed behind the chips, the block keeping watch in rotation so the owner can sleep

works.t: The Crypto Kid on the Roof
works.s: His rig heats the entire building through the winter by accident. The Bronx, nineteen years old, tenants who used to complain now bringing food
One bamboo pole turns a hundred birds into a single body. A Bushwick roof, a grandson on the ladder, the block circled from above
1657, Queens farmers signing a letter defending their neighbors' right to worship, candlelight on a plank table. Religious freedom drafted in a farmhouse before the nation existed

works.t: The Swan of the Boat Pond
works.s: A silver swan escorts becalmed sailboats back to their child captains. Neck lowered in a bow to each skipper, a tiny armada of sails following her wake
Elevators docking, the second coffee, markets opening with a bell somebody still gets to ring. Delivery bikes threading the settled grid
Groceries, lotto, hot food, cold beer, six fonts, zero lies. The yellow awning glows at night like a marquee for everything you need at 2am
Locals sidestep a square of sidewalk for reasons they cannot explain. Six floors of air conditioners, one wet ring, one visitor taking it directly
One in ten thousand, and he knows it. The grays pretend not to care, the joggers reroute daily
One midnight crossing, a cargo of gullwings, every door raised. Braided light trails behind the wake, a deckhand walking the rows with a lantern

works.t: Jadwiga Novotny, a diabetic rationing supplies on the fifteenth of the month
works.s: Polite is the coat she wears over being furious about the fifteenth. She explains the condition again, twice, to a professional watching the clock
The sommelier describes an orange wine like a weather event. Two skeptics taste it and quietly convert

works.t: Rocco Marchetti, a person who has never once posted their own face
works.s: Rocco has never once posted his own face. A bank form half filled in where the name goes

works.t: The Data Centre in the Church Basement
works.s: A whole neighbourhood's memory lives under the sanctuary floor. Harlem, a pastor in shirtsleeves, a cable in each hand and the servers humming
Great houses lend couture like library books now. A Bronx teenager checks out a bar jacket for her interview and returns it with the luck sewn in
It levitates on marble in a halo of light that hides the price. Worshipped by influencers, crowned with acai, compostable cup and all
Fulton Street stopped walking to watch a puffer become a ballgown. Sixteen years old, pins in her mouth, a train of goose down
The summer of 1936, eleven vast public pools opened in one season, ten thousand swimmers at the first whistle. The grandest public gift ever poured in concrete and chlorine
An octopus furnace in the cellar is a small dragon in an iron shell. A ten year old feeds it coal on cold mornings, a partnership of solemn nods
He throws the ball for himself and sprints under it every time. Sheep Meadow at noon, quilted coat, a crowd of real dogs studying the technique

works.t: Sami Demir, a person who tracked one piece through eleven owners
works.s: Sami tracked one piece through eleven owners. A box of receipts going back to 2017, the eleven

works.t: Shinji Cheung, a man who sculpts in a headset in a Flatiron loft
works.s: Shinji sculpts in a headset in a Flatiron loft. A lenticular print shifting in the light on the wall
He points down the block from his folding chair and everything it used to be rises translucent above the street. A teenager is actually listening, so the trolley runs again

works.t: The Chinese Grandfather at the Card Table
works.s: Their game has run daily in that pavilion since 1994. Sunset Park, six men in their eighties, and today a woman was let in

works.t: Zainab Owusu, a plotter operator feeding paper into a machine from 1965
works.s: Zainab feeds paper into a machine from 1965. A pen plotter with paper feeding, the rhythm unchanged

works.t: Adjoa Adeyemi, a person who has kept every receipt since 2017
works.s: Adjoa has kept every receipt since 2017. A ruled ledger open under one lamp, the rules blank

works.t: The Dance That Took the Platform
works.s: Nine hours to cross the city, three days to reach Lagos and Seoul. Broadway Junction, a kid killing time before the J, who has told nobody it was him

works.t: The Punk Show in the Basement
works.s: Sound in here is dense enough to hold the crowd off the floor. Bushwick, six inches of air under everybody, a singer who just noticed

works.t: Grigore Kaczmarek, a man who has commuted through this terminal and eaten here since 1979
works.s: He has eaten at this counter since 1979 and told nobody. A counter under the vaults, a bowl before the train, forty seven winters
The hundred year window serves its line under summer twilight. The paper cup is squeezed inside out on the curb, per regulation

works.t: Aminata Adeyemi, a woman who makes the whitefish salad by feel and never measures
works.s: Measuring is for people who have not made it ten thousand times. Reaching into a barrel to the elbow, under a ceiling of hanging salamis
The keeper of Robbins Reef rows her children to school across the harbor at dawn, the light behind her kept alone. Fifty sailors alive because of her lamp, the small boat steady in the ferry's wake

works.t: Tova Rosenblatt, a person who found a lost piece in a dead wallet
works.s: Tova found a lost piece in a dead wallet. A long library table covered in printouts tracing it

works.t: Hyun-woo Kobayashi, a man who has been here thirty one years and cannot vote
works.s: Thirty one years of paying in and no line on any ballot. He walks out of the building either way, and buys the coffee
Golden hour on the pier where generations found family. Voguing silhouettes against the sunset river, the water holding all of it gently

works.t: The Church of the Clean Render
works.s: Their discipline is the unfiltered face, layer switched all the way off. A plain room, enormous singing, and four dozen people looking directly at each other for ninety minutes
Each spring the block repaints the fading mural of its beloved before the colors can leave. A teenager steadying the ladder learns the face by brushstroke
The last one glows on its corner like a shrine. A teenager approaches as an archaeologist while grandma demonstrates the ritual of the quarter
Golden hour traffic and she kneels the bus for a rider with a walker. Kind tired eyes in the mirror, the crosstown route run like a promise
Goggles on, ears streaming, riding the bridge bike lane like a fighter pilot. Cyclists grinning as they pass, tongue at full sail

works.t: Chidi Sy, a longevity clinic patient with a full protocol and no friends
