works.s: Being the strong one has no off switch and no end date. He copies the word down phonetically while the doctor keeps talking, notebook on his knee
They got the ending right for the first time at seven in the morning. A Queens parking lot, a marching band, one clean last chord
Coats sorted themselves by warmth as the line got longer. Sidewalk rack, each collar lighting as its person steps up, breath in the cold
He gives the entire pole his whole spine while five hands hover homeless. The straps watch in judgment, and the car rides in ancient fury

works.t: Andre Hollins, a pool hall owner with a room of green felt
works.s: Green felt holds a room together better than most public policy. Closing up, the lights going off in sequence over an empty green table
A ceiling forest of piñatas and foil balloons, streamers by the mile. A kid chooses the birthday donkey with terrible gravity
The bell rang for a decision nobody had announced yet. Morning light on white stone, a cupola, every pigeon in the park up
Escaped parrots and machine mimics trade vocabularies on a Bushwick fire escape. The birds learn dial tones, the machines learn Spanish curses, the dawn chorus goes untranslatable
Brass tubes connect every bodega on the hill at ninety miles an hour. A loosie, a lime, a spare key, a plate for somebody's mother, and a fifteen year old dispatcher
Nine relatives landed unannounced and the table simply got longer. A small Queens kitchen, suitcases still by the door, a plate for everyone
Something he painted years ago leaves today for the rest of the country. A Queens yard fence at dawn, coffee, a car rolling west

works.t: The Last Watch of the Woolworth Owls
works.s: The stone owls keep the last watch of the night shift together. Shoulder to shoulder against the pre dawn, heads turning one final quarter turn as the sun breaks
The oldest cedar in Tribeca teaches one doctrine: water wants to come down well. Tenants swear their showers fall patiently, like water that has been somewhere and thought about it

works.t: The Eighty Eight on the FDR
works.s: Eighty eight on an empty FDR opens the road like a zipper. Three in the morning, tail lights stretched to ribbon, the East River frozen mid ripple

works.t: Sohail Rahman, a landlord's son who has started to understand the ledger
works.s: He grew up on the income side of the ledger and has started reading it. His room has a window, and the window faces a brick wall

works.t: The Boy Whose Whole Class Is In One Chat
works.s: Leaving the group chat is socially identical to leaving the borough. On a stoop of bowed heads, his is the one face turned to the sky
A flock in matching lanyards migrates through midtown at lunch, salads held like briefcases. One leader carries the corporate card, glowing with borrowed power

works.t: The Man Who Was in a Video He Was Never In
works.s: The floor of what is true gave way, and he went through it first. Wendell carries a folder of timestamps everywhere, the only solid man on a wall of light
A retired keeper finds an eye flower budding at the focus of the museum's great Fresnel lens, and the glass wakes to throw one slow beam across the room. The lights are in on it now
Old 42nd Street at full neon sleaze, grindhouse marquees stacked three deep. Popcorn and hustle and a saxophone somewhere, every sign buzzing a different pink
The kings held court on a subway bench, black books passed like scripture. Their trains rolled past as moving galleries of their own work
Thirty years at one corner, and now the white gloves pass like a torch. The new guard's first solo stop lands perfectly while the old one watches from the curb
The shapeshifter that has worn more routes than any line, crossing its own history daily. Orange, and amused by its own map
The tray comes out of the oven like treasure because it is. Golden patties, coco bread stacked high, Flatbush fed properly
A nine year old with a notebook keeps the only accurate forecast up here. She asks the gargoyle, watches the bees, listens to the tank, and writes it down
Done for forty one minutes, still occupying the only working dryer. The line debates the touching law like a supreme court

works.t: Tarek Ansari, a cook who came here after his own kitchen closed
works.s: His kitchen closed and he found another one still lit. Leaning through a lit window onto an empty street, coat over kitchen whites

works.t: The Second Line Through Bed Stuy
works.s: A crowd doubles every block behind the brass band. Marcy on a Sunday, and the trumpet player at the front never looks back
Nobody is watching, which is exactly why the shots count. A Brooklyn court at six, fog still on the asphalt, free throws
This machine lends against a future you have not earned yet. Bus fare home for a stranded student, drawn on a job she has not been offered
The elevator falls eighteen stories to a platform inside the mountain itself. The bedrock sweats cool and the train arrives like a vein of light through stone
The Union Square greenmarket breaks down at six, farmers stacking crates and hosing the cobbles. One late shopper scores the last peaches at a wave of the hand while the sparrows audit the sweep

works.t: Kelvin Odom, a man who keeps two phones for two people
works.s: Kelvin keeps two phones for two people. A hotel corridor and a costume half on, phone one

works.t: Deirdre Donnelly, a person who won big early and has been chasing it since
works.s: Deirdre won big early and has been chasing it since. A phone put down and picked up again, chasing
Two strangers compare ailments and remedies with total candor while the line inches forward. More healing happens in the line than in the bag

works.t: The Look That Left the Store
works.s: An outfit walked out of the window with nobody inside it. Soho cobblestones, three blocks gone before anyone noticed, tourists parting around ivory
Souvlaki smoke drifts over the beer gardens toward the studio stage doors. Greek grandmothers water gardens beside filmmakers hauling lights, and both crews respect the other's craft

works.t: The Woman Who Verifies for a Living
works.s: Verification pays well and has cost her every source she used to trust. Leaning back from the panels, she checks it twice and files no verdict

works.t: Suresh Mahadevan, a promoter who has been wrong about the future many times
works.s: Wrong about the future often enough to know it does not matter. A canopy in the rain, a stamped hand, a flight case with no corners
Bent, drained, flat on the platform edge under one shaft of grate light. The stripe catches a last dull rainbow before the train's wind takes it

works.t: The Woman Who Reads the MRI Like a Map
works.s: She reads the whole life in the scan, not the disease. Manhattan, something true said out loud that never made the report
It looks like an inch deep and has ended careers. Locals guard the shoreline like park rangers

works.t: Bernice Starks, an engineer in a cage of servers on Hudson Street at three in the morning
works.s: Bernice is an engineer in a cage of servers on Hudson Street at three in the morning. A hash written by hand on a card
Pulled apart in slow motion, ruby guava strings bridging the golden halves. The napkin never stood a chance
Between the chips and the lottery terminal, the future takes cash. A paper flower instead of a receipt, and one very confused customer

works.t: Trina Sealy, a photographer who wrote her own editorial when nobody would publish it
works.s: Trina wrote her own editorial when nobody would publish it. A big inkjet printing one physical, the run of one

works.t: Aaliyah Ballard, a lawyer trying to explain what is being sold
works.s: Aaliyah is a lawyer trying to explain what is being sold. A keyboard with the letters worn off from the memo
One continuous coat of white over the outlet, the hinge, the roach, and the doorbell. Decades of layers at every chip, and the flowers still bloom through

works.t: Ibrahim Camara, a man who books the impossible table for other people for a fee
works.s: He knows which four top to hold and exactly who wants it. Book opens at ten sharp, a fee, a four top held all night, no apprentice
Ink blinked once and neither of them moved. A Ridgewood chair, a forearm, a flower the artist did not finish alone
Ties tucked into pants, a beer cooler at third base, dusk on the diamond. The skyline watches the outfield while office rivalries settle honestly

works.t: Yangzom Gurung, a dispatcher who runs a whole borough by radio
works.s: Runs a borough by radio and has never written any of it down. Sunrise exactly, a booth on a bridge, a river going from grey to gold

works.t: The Chef Who Made Them Come to Her
works.s: She refuses to be the story, so the food carries it alone. Four months of waiting seated behind her, a pass, a headset, a plate

works.t: Bogdan Danylchenko, a man who moved his whole life to the second floor
works.s: Moving upstairs was not a renovation, it was a forecast. He swims over what used to be his own front steps

works.t: The Man Who Planted a Tree for Everyone He Lost
works.s: Four hundred and eleven street trees, one for each person gone. Queens at dawn, the newest one going in, the block out with water

works.t: The Most Trusted Woman on the Block
works.s: The block trusts her stamp more than it trusts the state. She cannot retire because nobody has been trained to take the desk

works.t: Everton Toussaint, a night security guard doing a route he could walk asleep
works.s: Quiet fury, immaculate manners, and a wage that matches neither. A lantern in a tunnel, a humming rail, a headlight not yet around the curve
A neon lit sticker shop the width of a hallway glows between a locksmith and a church. All three fix things
Crushed cars sing better than they ever drove. A Willets Point yard at sunset, stacked window frames, stadium lights coming on behind
Concrete started picking corners and enjoying itself. Lower East Side park, a man in his fifties reaching, diamonds of fence shadow
The hundred year wait ended on new year's day as crowds flooded the gleaming new station. Grandparents touching the tilework their grandparents were promised

works.t: Vesna Wozniak, a woman who reads official letters aloud for her neighbours
works.s: She explains the same sentence to the ninth person before lunch. Nobody pays her for it, and the call log is in her own handwriting

works.t: Feng Ishikawa, a man who calls it a community and means it
works.s: He calls it a community, and the terrible part is that he means it. The second before checking, a kitchen table, a hand not yet on the phone

works.t: Lian Chow, a ferry captain reading a changed river
works.s: She learned one river and now runs a different one. Two in the morning, a basement, a pump, and one flashlight

works.t: Tomasz Horvat, a man on year nine of a three year process
works.s: Home is a place that kept moving while he stood completely still. Ninth in a line that reaches the corner, holding a soft folder

works.t: Rohan Bonaparte, a man who covers the wall of his studio in contact sheets
works.s: Rohan covers the studio wall in contact sheets. A paper backdrop and a strobe under all of it
Picture day in the gym, the comb line, a crooked collar fixed by a stranger's mom. One chipped tooth grin about to become the year's most treasured artifact
On his last shift the whole collection turns toward the door. Painted eyes, marble faces, gilded saints, and a man sitting down on the bench to weep
Nothing is really deleted, it just falls somewhere quieter. A Chelsea data floor, cold aisle light, glowing paper drifting down like snow

works.t: The Optometrist Who Corrects for Beauty
works.s: Lenses ground here correct for what is good about where you live. Bay Ridge, an old man in a trial pair turning toward the window

works.t: Lloyd Charlemagne, a man who found his real friends here
works.s: Lloyd found his real friends here. Twelve name tags on a table, nine of them friends

works.t: Nechama Landau, a woman who runs the box office of a theatre older than her family here
works.s: This theatre is older than her family's whole history in the country. A box office cage pulled halfway down, a propped load in door

works.t: The Hustle That Became the Institution
works.s: A folding table ran long enough for the city to give it a plaque. The founder started it to survive and cannot work out how to feel

works.t: Octavio Sandoval, an annotation team lead in a converted warehouse floor
works.s: Four hundred times he has corrected the same error, and it will come back. What he wants is small: one door in the building carrying his own name

works.t: The Block That Turned Down the Volume
works.s: Quiet after eleven became an agreement and then became a dome. Astoria, a driver idling at the edge of it with his bass up

works.t: Roisin Wren, a portrait photographer in Harlem with a paper backdrop
works.s: Roisin shoots portraits in Harlem with a paper backdrop. A big inkjet printing one physical of each
August's moon pulls the ancient fish up from under the bridges. One silver back breaks the surface, the Hudson remembering its giants

works.t: Mendel Feldman, an asylum seeker with a hearing date and a good coat
works.s: Three sentences decide it, so he says them a hundred times a night. Nobody has asked him how he is since the airport
It skipped the Hudson like a stone and left rings from nineteen twenty. Dawn, a ferry crowd filming from the rail, the Palisades gone pink behind them

works.t: Rupert Fairweather, a man who sold his to pay a hospital bill
works.s: Rupert sold his to pay a hospital bill. A laptop turned around toward somebody, the bill on screen

works.t: Gus Ferrante, a busboy who knows which table belongs to which family
works.s: He knows which table belongs to which family and says nothing about either. The regular walks in, the room turns, and four plates leave his arm
Every empty chair fills with whoever used to sit there. A Corona Sunday, the table extending down the hallway, the matriarch cooking in two decades at once

works.t: Shoshana Zilberman, an artist waiting in a hallway to be interviewed for the first time
works.s: Shoshana is waiting to be interviewed for the first time in her life. A lanyard with a blank badge, a hallway that hums
Green water and salt haze made the great statue a sister. Rough nights only, a torch of bioluminescence raised, the channel between them lit like an aisle

works.t: Lhakpa Gurung, a man who borrowed against a piece and is now watching the price
works.s: Lhakpa borrowed against a piece and is watching the price. A phone face down under one flat hand, watching anyway
Homesickness got heavy enough to become geology. Corona Park, a small snow capped volcano, Sunday families eating in air that smells of Ecuador

works.t: Analiza Tsering, a fan account admin who is more famous than she is
works.s: Her fan account outgrew the person the account is about. At the kitchen table she tries to explain the job to her mother

works.t: Faige Shulman, a woman who keeps her contemporaneous notes in the description of every piece
works.s: Faige keeps her contemporaneous notes in the description of every piece. A chain link fence with prints wired to it
She wheels him to his old corner so he can watch the block wake up, tucking the blanket without being asked. His face lights like a boy's, the corner remembers him too

works.t: Yvonne Jean-Baptiste, a woman who shoots long exposures from a DUMBO rooftop
works.s: Yvonne shoots long exposures from a DUMBO rooftop. A changing bag with hands inside on the way up

works.t: Feng Tran-Wu, a curator who reads code before looking at pictures
works.s: Feng reads code before looking at pictures. A flat file of prints and a loupe, the code approved

works.t: Mamadou Camara, a seminar host with a rented room and a hundred chairs
works.s: Filling a hundred chairs pays better than anything he was ever trained for. A sofa too big for the room, a family told at the table
Seven cooling pies nobody ordered and a 3am accounting. The steam rises in question marks, and he leans on the counter and reads them

works.t: Kelvin Hollins, a man whose piece was removed from a platform and later reinstated
works.s: Kelvin's piece was removed from a platform and later reinstated. A chain link fence with prints wired to it

works.t: The Mirror That Shows the Neighborhood
works.s: A barbershop mirror shows the block instead of the customer, forty years deep. You sit down for a fade and watch the storefronts change and change back, chair doing the work

works.t: Leyla Ansari, a woman who built a virtual model who never ages
works.s: Leyla built a virtual model who never ages. A handheld scanning rig beside the monitor

works.t: Nechama Lieberman, a roofer in August with tar and no shade
works.s: Being believed the first time would save about four hours a week. An open panel of a hundred wires, and a skyline of lit windows

works.t: The One Who Went and Came Back
works.s: Nine years over there, and he has just come back across the water. Everything is different and he is fine, and his sister is running down the Bay Ridge pier

works.t: Faige Lieberman, a hospice aide who has done this ninety times
works.s: Ninety times through the last week of a life, and she still laughs. A joke passes between two people and stays inside that room

works.t: Lian Kwon, a livestream gift farmer working an eleven hour stream
works.s: Eleven hours of being delightful is a shift, not a personality. One comment lands hard, and the closet behind her holds a single outfit

works.t: The Rider Who Knows the City Better Than Any Map
works.s: Boubacar has crossed this bridge four hundred times and never once been hired. Every route he ever rode burns behind him as one long line

works.t: Tova Landau, a woman who shoots portraits of artists in their own doorways
works.s: Tova shoots portraits of artists in their own doorways. A changing bag with hands inside between visits
She resets loose tiles and the walls pay her back in family. Three generations of setters at work in the tesserae, one century of grout
He sorts the bottles by value with real expertise and no audience. Bowery, a shopping cart, one stranger who actually stopped to listen
Brim angle on this Bronx corner works as a barometer for the block. Every brim tilts up two degrees the night the hospital sends the coach home healthy

works.t: Andre Whitlock, a barber whose chair his father stood behind
works.s: His father stood behind this chair, and the chair has not moved. Putting on his father's jacket, now two sizes too generous, in the same room
She beat three teenagers in a row and let them keep their dignity. Coney Island, a painted concrete wall, a woman in her sixties not gloating
Cashed and fanned once in private, one bill peeled for mom by unwritten law. The bodega witnessing the oldest tax in the city paid proudly
The white pail unfolds origami style in mid air, noodles suspended like calligraphy. The wire handle held, it always holds

works.t: Rania Zaman, a woman who has memorized the entire housing code
works.s: Chapter and verse of the housing code, held in one woman's head. Tonight she puts a nail in the wall, which is a kind of forecast
It added two minutes and told the only useful lie of the day. A sprinting teenager clearing the doors, the whole platform a smear behind her sneakers
Inside liberty's crown at dawn, copper ribs glowing green gold around the small windows. The view the statue keeps for herself

works.t: Dulce Bustamante, a woman who keeps the funeral programs of a whole congregation
works.s: A whole congregation is filed by hand in her front room. She holds a photograph up against the place it was taken, matching brick

works.t: The Elevator Mechanic Who Talks Them Down
works.s: He negotiates with the car instead of repairing it. Midtown machine room, a stuck car listening, passengers hearing one side of the talk
The gate rolls down at ten and the night shift of painters clocks in. One masterpiece burner over years of tags, the streetlight raking every ridge

works.t: The Rent Party of the Whole City
works.s: To celebrate, the city throws itself a rent party in the old style. Every stoop a stage, the buried streams for ice, the old reliquary ball for the light
Passengers stood calm on the wings while ferries converged from every direction. The impossible rendered gently, the river holding everyone up
She holds the skyline upside down and does not shake. A Greenpoint pier, two hands on planking, Manhattan hanging from the sky
She could not get the last line out, so it waited. A room gone quiet and patient, disco ball scatter on every wall
He hands her back before the mother finishes turning around. A Bronx stoop rail, a slipped toddler, two arms already there

works.t: The Taxi With One Last Fare
works.s: She still waits at a stand that closed thirty years ago. A retired yellow cab out of Long Island City, one glowing meter
A retired doorman orders two coffees every morning and hands the second to whoever looks like the night was long. The cart man builds that one sweeter

works.t: The Day the El Came Down
works.s: The elevated comes down and sunlight hits Third Avenue for the first time in fifty years. An old waiter looks up at a sky he had taken on faith
